gateflrgateflr If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it noticesgateflr If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it notices — HOLD: FILE: measured during the R1+R2 regression review — Found by the flagship while reviewing the R1 and R2 regression evidence. The new gate-2 block guards itself: its floors, its named-row greps and its positive control are all INSIDE the block. Delete the block and every one of those guards disappears with it, while the gate still reports PASS - nothing outside floors gate 2's check count. hlenhlen Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit)hlen Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit) — HOLD: census done; promote to a FIX round? — Opened from the b75 refutation, then characterized by census. A device handler that switches on the address and cannot service a width will read or write only the first register of an 8-byte access. MEASURED SCOPE: 62 spanning-capable handlers of 167 registered; 20 on machines this project boots. TWO BOOTED MACHINES ARE PROVABLY IMMUNE - SH-4 has no 8-byte access at all (fmov.d is two 4-byte accesses) and MIPS32/R3000A treats LD/SD as reserved, so landisk and pmax cannot produce the access. NO CONVENTION EXISTS in the tree: no helper, no macro, no rule - only three hand-rolled decompositions that are all big-endian-specific and that disagree with each other about the else branch, so there is no single idiom to copy. FIRST WITNESS NAMED: dev_irqc on testarm, the only spanning-capable device on that machine, where the two halves of one aligned 8-byte access have OPPOSITE legal directions (status is read-only, mask is write-only), which makes the miss unambiguous. DETECTOR SHAPE: an offline differential in the diff_*.c family - no boot, no rig, no serialization.held
Assessment (initial problem)✓2026-08-22 — CLOSE (assess). Promote SELECTIVELY, never as a sweep: only handlers where a wrong length is issuable through real decode on a witnessable machine AND produces wrong data or state; each instance is its own round. A census promoted wholesale is how scope balloons.✓2026-08-15 — CONFIRMED — CENSUS: 118 files, 62 spanning-capable handlers, 20 on booted machines. mrwstore2mrwstore2 A straddling store whose tail faults makes an MMIO head see the write twicemrwstore2 A straddling store whose tail faults makes an MMIO head see the write twice — commits: 0447c2e — HOLD: *** THE OLD BLOCKING REASON IS REFUTED AND WAS AN L4 -- corrected 2026-08-26. *** It read 'the fix may itself DIVERGE from real hardware'. **A fix cannot diverge, because the behaviour is PERMITTED and never REQUIRED.** Four PowerPC manuals are now local in `_scratchpad/` (OEA Book III v2.01, VEA Book II v2.01, MPCFPE32B Rev 2 -- the 32-bit PEM covering the PPC750 this row's witness uses -- and the 2005 32/64-bit PEM), fetched and extracted with the same pdftotext used for ddi0100i.txt. PEM 3.2.2 / Book II 2.1: a misaligned store is not atomic, so it falls in the 'any other load or store instruction MAY be partially executed and then aborted... and then re-executed' bucket; 6.1.4 says 'some bytes just before the boundary may have been updated'. **So an emulator that never partially executes is conformant under every one of them -- the INTERSECTION of both readings, not a divergence from either.** *** AND THE MANUALS DISAGREE ON THE CASE THIS ROW IS ACTUALLY ABOUT, recorded as an honest UNKNOWN rather than settled by the stronger document: *** Book III v2.01 4.2.4.1 says that for an access whose first byte is Caching-Inhibited AND Guarded -- exactly the MMIO-head shape here -- a DSI means 'the portion of the storage operand that is in Caching Inhibited and Guarded storage is NOT accessed', i.e. the device write must not happen. The PEM contains no such rule and its 6.1.4 explicitly permits the head bytes to have been updated. Whether a real PPC750 suppresses the device write is NOT established. THE REASONS THAT SURVIVE and on which this row stays filed: REACHABILITY (zero straddling stores measured across three real boots) and SEVERITY (a duplicated device write -- guest-visible, no host kill, no memory-safety consequence; both PowerPC and ARM put the burden on software). *** SCOPE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE BLOCKER: 'memory_rw is the choke point' is FALSE FOR THE CLASS. *** stmw/stswi/lmw/lswi and ARM's bdt_store each loop and return on the first failing element, so they have the identical partial-completion-across-a-fault property at the INSTRUCTION level, entirely outside memory_rw -- and PEM 6.1.4's first bullet is about exactly those. **A memory_rw fix would be a partial fix that reads as a complete one**, which is the argument for filing this properly rather than shipping a round a future reader mistakes for closure. TWO SIDE-EFFECT CAUTIONS FROM A PRIOR SEAT MEASURED ABSENT IN THIS TREE: FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS returns before every SPR write and before ppc_exception(), and there is NO R/C writeback on PPC at all -- so the recorded warning about PPC603 software reload describes hazards that do not exist here. FILED SEPARATELY, all from the same reading: `X(stvx)` does a raw 16-byte memory_rw with no `EA & ~0xF` mask (a second straddling producer, and a divergence in its own right); diff_memory_rw.c has a coverage hole exactly at this row's shape (device head + FAULTING tail); and memory_ppc.c:302-305 is an unlatched guest-drivable fatal(), one per translation fault -- the floodclass shape #464 just closed six of.held

THE WITNESS: unmodified in-tree `testppc` (-E testppc -C PPC750 -M 32), cold debugger, real guest instructions, real decode, real memory_rw. A PPC guest sets DBAT0 over a 128 KB window, sets MSR[DR]=1, and executes `stw r6,0(r5)` with r5 = 0x1201fffe -- unaligned, crossing the 1 KB split granule. Head (2 bytes) reaches the in-tree `fb` device; tail (2 bytes) has no BAT and no PTE, so a real DSI fires; a planted `rfi` at the DSI vector is the GUEST'S OWN restart. The same instruction re-executes, unbounded. Counters: one architectural store, FOUR device writes. **The trace is from a fully stock HEAD binary with zero instrumentation** -- the counters only counted. Controls all green: liveness (RAM through the same decode), DEVICE SIGNATURE (same program, only DBAT0L changed: PA->device reads back 0x3344, PA->no device reads back 0x0000), and a negative control two bytes lower that does not split. CLAIM 1 -- 'not introduced by #430' -- MEASURED FALSE. Built from `git show 2458cfb^:src/cpus/memory_rw.c`, stock otherwise: the same guest program produces NO exception, NO restart, ONE device write. Pre-#430 the tail was silently mis-applied to the physically-following location -- the defect #430 fixed -- so there was nothing to restart. **#430 CREATED the fault, and the double-application is a direct consequence of it.** CLAIM 2 -- 'the memblock split has had this property all along' -- MEASURED FALSE, twice. Post-#430 the memblock split can only fire on PHYSICAL accesses (a translated 4 KB write across 1 MB costs 4 translations / 4 host lookups; PHYSICAL costs 0 / 2), and its head can NEVER be a device in either version because device dispatch `goto do_return_ok`s first -- measured with a device straddling the memblock boundary. CLAIM 3 -- '256x' -- MEASURED WRONG: it is **1024x**. The granule was measured by walking offsets, not read: MRW_SPLIT_MASK is 0x3ff, so 1 MB / 1024 = 1024. The 256 came from comparing 1 MB to a 4 KB page -- the granule this split does not use. *** THE SAME WRONG NUMBER WAS ALSO IN THE SOURCE, at memory_rw.c's own 'one boundary in 256' comment: ONE mis-derived constant became TWO records defects, and the row repeated it as a severity argument. Both corrected. *** REACHABILITY IS FAR NARROWER THAN THE ROW IMPLIES, and this is why it re-ranks DOWN: * ONLY PowerPC can emit a straddling store at all. MIPS (AdES; swl/swr do an ALIGNED RMW), ARM, SH, M88K and Alpha all force alignment -- each checked in source. PPC's `if (addr & (LS_SIZE-1))` at cpu_ppc_instr_loadstore.c:229 is a FAST-PATH BAIL-OUT, not an exception, so the generic path passes the unaligned address through. * PPC is also the ONLY family whose device-failure path can restart: memory_rw's device-failure arm raises an exception only under #ifdef MEM_MIPS / #ifdef MEM_M88K. * THREE REAL GUEST BOOTS, instrumented: OpenBSD/pmax to root login, OpenBSD/luna88k to `login:`, NetBSD/macppc to the root-device prompt -- **ZERO straddling stores from guest code**. The seat first read macppc's 95 split-loop writes as guest activity and REFUTED ITSELF by logging the addresses: all are len=65536 at pc=0x0, i.e. file_elf.c:448's loader chunks running before any guest instruction. * Of the 1024 offsets in a granule only ELEVEN (0x3f9..0x3ff) can start a straddling 2/4/8-byte access, and the head's device offset is always within 7 bytes BELOW a 1 KB boundary -- so a register at offset 0x00/0x10/0x20 can never be a straddle head. *** AND THE FIX MAY ITSELF BE WRONG. *** Partial completion on a page-crossing misaligned store, with restart re-applying the first part, is what real PowerPC hardware does -- so gxemul may be CORRECT here and a fix may introduce a divergence. There is no PowerPC manual in _scratchpad/ (ARM, MIPS and m88k only), so the seat stated that as REASONING, NOT A CITATION -- the same trap CLAUDE.md records for SH. **Obtain a PPC manual before any edit.** The minimal fix, if one is wanted: a dry-run pre-pass on WRITES only, walking the chunks with FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS and committing only if all translate. Zero cost on the hot path -- it sits inside the `while (len > granule - offset)` body, which no aligned access enters. Watch TLB-miss handlers with side effects (PPC603 software reload) and do not let the dry run update referenced/changed bits. mrwstore2_rung3.py is close to shippable as a regress detector; its controls already satisfy the liveness and device-signature clauses. — evidence: _scratchpad/ (mrwstore2_rung3.py, sig.py, probe_mrwstore2.c)·······

Four defects are now specifiable. (1) SS7.3.41 bit 6: FREERUN wraps to FFFFFFh and keeps counting; PERIODIC reloads TimerNLoad; the clock source is bits 3:2 alone, identical in both. reload_timer_value() computes one rate and hands it to a repeating timer -- the PERIODIC cadence unconditionally -- so a FREERUN timer is too fast by up to 2^24/load. (2) TimerNValue is READ-ONLY (SS7.3.38/7.3.40) but the model accepts a guest write, and TIMER_1_CLEAR has NO writeflag test, so a guest READ of a write-only register reloads the counter and deasserts the IRQ. (3) Reset values diverge: hardware gives CONTROL 0x00 and LOAD 0, the model gives TIMER_MODE_PERIODIC and TIMER_MAX_VAL -- and this is the model bug #432's first draft mistakenly cited as evidence for its own zero mapping. (4) The random() counter model is now fully specified by SS7.3.40 + SS7.3.41 bit 7: a 24-bit down-counter, readable any time, RETAINED across disable and resuming on re-enable. The author's TODO is discharged; only a rig is missing. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260815_221232/✓2026-08-16 — MANUAL — Expand the item: external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model belong in it alongside the four already listed. Research (fix proposals)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** REPRODUCED AT RUNG 3, AND MY OWN PREMISE FOR THE TASK WAS WRONG. *** I briefed the measure seat that NO rig reaches the 8253 -- only algor/cobalt/evbmips/iyonix via bus_isa -- and that a rung-4 witness therefore almost certainly did not exist. HALF FALSE, and the false half is what made rung 3 reachable. `bus_isa_init` has SIX callers outside src/machines/: bus_pci.c:476 and :1060, dev_eagle.c:160,172, dev_lca.c:376, dev_prep.c:80. My grep looked only at src/machines/ and bus_*.c and I reported the subset as the whole. **cats** reaches the 8253 through machine_cats.c -> dev_footbridge.c:730 (bus_pci_add "ali_m1543") -> bus_pci.c:459/476, at isa_portbase 0x7c000000. Verified here independently. THE WITNESS: a cold-debugger probe on UNMODIFIED `-E cats`, the same mechanics as footbridge_sites_probe.py. Pre-fix and post-fix binaries from the same tree, same script: C1 liveness 0x11223344 both RAM through the same decode A1 device signature 0xAA both see below T1 negative control halts at paddr=0x0c000043, MMU-on cannot reach it D0 count 0 -> hz 0 Hz -> 18 Hz the device's own report G0 guest-visible IRR 0x0 -> 0x1 after a 1.9 s free-run D1 positive control count 4608 -> 259 Hz, IRR=0x1, identical both ways All four controls green in BOTH runs; only the two symptom rows move. THE DEVICE SIGNATURE IS A VALUE RAM CANNOT PRODUCE, and it was designed against the exact trap that ate the footbridge probe's first draft. The guest writes 0xAA then 0x55 to the SAME address in 16-bit mode, writes the MODE register (a different address), then reads back and gets 0xAA -- the byte from two writes ago. RAM returns 0x55. Nonzero deliberately, because 0x0 is what an ABSENT device looks like. TWO CAVEATS THE SEAT OWNED RATHER THAN HID: G0/G1 use a WALL-CLOCK window (1.9 s against a 55 ms correct period, ~34 chances), which is why the post-fix green is the settlement and not the window size; and its first T1 draft reported FAIL through a string-equality bug in its own script, which it found and fixed. All 27 instruction encodings were checked against the emulator's own disassembler before use -- the hand-assembled-encoding trap this project has hit four times. REACHABILITY, MEASURED: no guest in this tree programs count 0. Every PIT write in _guest-src-openbsd22/sys/ is TIMER_DIV(x) (never 0) or 0xff/0xff, and no rig image boots an 8253 machine. A recollection that Linux's pit_shutdown() writes 0,0 was flagged RECALLED, UNVERIFIED rather than cited -- the right handling. *** BUT FINDING `pitflip` BELOW MANUFACTURES COUNT 0 FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER ASKS FOR IT, which changes the reachability picture entirely. *** MAPPINGS, measured not read: cats and netwinder 0x7c000040; malta/maltabe 0x18000040; cobalt 0x10000040; iyonix 0x90000040; absent on prep, mvmeppc, algor, arc. THE FIX is one line -- hz = (int)(I8253_TIMER_FREQ / 65536.0 + 0.5) -> 18 -- and d->hz[] is read only at :133/137/140, all inside the MSB arm, so the blast radius is that arm. *** DO NOT GENERALISE BY ANALOGY: dev_rtc.c:129 and dev_mc146818.c:409 look identical and are CORRECT -- for those devices zero genuinely means 'off', and dev_rtc.c's comment records a prior round reasoning that through. The 8254 is the opposite case. *** Minor: int hz[3] rounds 18.2065 to 18 (-1.1%) while timer_add takes a double. — evidence: _scratchpad/t8253/ (pit8253_count0_probe.py, pit8253_site_probe.py)·······
Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** MERGE WITH pitlsb -- passes all three prongs, and #440 has just built the state the fix needs. *** Both are 'when is a counter load complete, and what rate does it imply', and both live in the SAME `case I8253_TIMER_MSB:` block (i8253zero = its `else hz = 0`; pitlsb = the fact that `case I8253_TIMER_LSB:` has no equivalent). Same device, one oracle (the device's own `[ 8253: counter %i set to %i (%i Hz) ]`), and ONE restructure fixes both: hoist the recompute + timer_add/timer_update_frequency into a helper called under a 'load complete per programmed format' predicate, with count == 0 => 65536. *** THE SEQUENCING IS NOW FORCED, which is information the cluster panel did not have: *** #440 introduces wr_msb[3], a per-counter write flip-flop. That IS the completeness predicate the merged fix needs. Designing this before #440 would have had to invent it; after #440 it is free. A TRAP TO WRITE INTO THE BRIEF: do NOT simply recompute in both arms. In 16-bit format the LSB half must NOT recompute, because `counter` then holds (stale_high | new_low) -- that would call timer_update_frequency with a garbage rate, re-introducing precisely the transient-wrong-hz that pitflip was filed for. *** AND THIS ROW'S WITNESS IS NOT RE-RUNNABLE. *** 1ce189c ('i8253zero REPRODUCED at rung 3') changed tools/pipeline/ledger.json ONLY -- no probe script -- and the row's witness field is None. That rung-3 result exists as a transcript. Before the merged round ships, its D0-equivalent row must exist AS A FILE, or the fix lands with a witness nobody can reproduce: the fifth vacuity class in its hardest-to-see shape, because a transcript LOOKS like evidence. Harm if reached: emulated clock frozen -- hz=0 -> timer_clamp_freq floors to TIMER_MIN_FREQUENCY = 1e-8 Hz, one tick per 3.17 years. — evidence: git show 1ce189c --stat; dev_8253.c I8253_TIMER_MSB arm·······

(Caveat recorded by the seat: that source is OpenBSD 2.2/mvme88k, the lineage, not the booting guest; the boot measurement is the evidence for the actual guest.) *** THE OLD COST NOTE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. *** 'Needs the translation walk' implies a CAPABILITY gap. **The walk exists** -- m88k_translate_v2p() at memory_m88k.c:103 -- **and is already side-effect-free under FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS** (:344 guards the PG_U/PG_M writeback, :374 returns before any PFSR/PFAR write), its flags already cover the probe's own selectors, and the SSR bit layout is in-tree. **And the driving probe SHAPE is already committed**: m8820x_sites_probe.py:159 ships a PROBE_SUPER row driven by one real guest instruction, ~3 s, no boot. *This is the `sh4dmacie` situation in reverse -- there the shape was missing and it was mis-read as a capability gap; here the shape was already there and nobody re-read the probe.* **WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS AN ORACLE, AND THE HOLD IS NOW CONDITIONAL ON IT:** translate_v2p exposes no BATC-vs-PATC-vs-walk distinction (needed for CMMU_SSR_BH) and none of the U/M/PROT/SO attributes SSR must carry; real probe semantics are supported only by DDB code reading those registers, which is evidence and not proof; and **there is no 88200/88204 manual in this project**. TRIGGER, on the SH4_VAL_NCLASS precedent: **if an 88200/88204 manual is obtained, this becomes a small round.** That converts an indefinite hold into a conditional one. *** AND THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS THE BETTER ONE, which is the strongest reason not to rank it: *** a dropped probe leaves SSR zero with the V bit clear -- a deterministic, DEFINED 'no valid translation'. Implementing without the manual would replace a defined conservative miss with an INVENTED answer that could steer the guest's paging. **That is the same reasoning used to decline `sh4aaalias` before the SH manual arrived -- and that one turned out to be a wrong finding.** The only known consumer prints a line in a debugger display, so a cosmetically wrong DDB line for a human is the entire measured consequence. WORTH ADDING CHEAPLY: one row asserting SSR == 0 after a probe, to pin the DELIBERATE behaviour that today rests on prose in two comments and no oracle at all.held

Denominators self-reported by the harnesses: diff_m8820x 46 rows + diff_m8invread 33 rows = 79, with two deliberate @@SELFCHECK@@ FAIL lines in each file as negative controls, so a raw grep of 2 IS the green baseline. *** THE CONTROLS ARE WHAT MAKE THIS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION, and they show the blindness is STRUCTURAL: *** M3 (`sar = 0`) reddens D1/D3, proving the harness CAN see a consumer-side SAR defect; M4 (drop the SAR store) reddens E7/E8/G6/G7, proving it CAN see a producer-side one. **Both ends are covered; only the SEAM is blind** -- because every SCR-flush row runs after `fresh()` (which memsets the device, so cpu_nr = cmmu_nr = 0) and issues from cpu0, and at (0,0) every candidate base for `regs` coincides. **M1 IS A LIVE-DEFECT CLASS ON THE SHIPPED RIG, NOT A SHAPE PIN**, and the seat verified the load-bearing fact from source rather than trusting a harness comment: `dev_luna88k.c:926-957` registers BOTH CMMUs on every boot, and `dev_m8820x.c:542-543` maps `addr2 & 1` -> cmmu_nr, so cmmu_nr = 1 is guest-addressable on every luna88k boot -- with the data CMMU taking 318,457 of 613,342 SAR writes (51.9%%). Under M1 **half the machine's PATC flushes never dispatch at all**, which is the silently-under-invalidating TLB the file's own comment calls 'not a cosmetic gap'. (M2, the `(cpu, d)` swap, is by contrast a shape pin: the booting rig is single-CPU.) *** THE COMPOSED ROW IS BUILT AND MEASURED -- THREE ROWS, EACH WITH ITS OWN KILL, NONE DECORATION: *** K1 (matching entry dropped) reddens under M1/M1b; K2 (non-matching entry retained) under M5; K3 (flush from a NON-OWNER cpu) under M2. **The two axes are independent: K1 does not catch M2 and K3 does not catch M1.** The original filing asked for 'cmmu_nr 1 AND from a non-owner CPU'; the measurement shows both halves are load-bearing and neither subsumes the other -- sharper than the filing knew. Goes in diff_m8invread.c, which has the two-cpu/two-cmmu fixture; ~20 lines; prototype committed to the artifact dir. The jazz leg is much weaker than filed: 64-bit store only (any 32-bit store bottoms out at 2.33e-7 Hz, 23x above floor). Same device, same class, same oracle, one fix design. MEASURED FALSE, found by the seat driving the pitlatch round: void debug(...) { ...; if ((quiet_mode && !ss) || v < 0) return; va_debug(...); } void fatal(...) { va_debug(...); } `debug()` carries an EARLY-OUT on quiet_mode and verbosity; `fatal()` has NONE. They are not the same function and never were. What I got right is that fatal() does not EXIT -- that part stands, and it was the point I was making each time. The seat replicated that loop byte-for-byte rather than paraphrasing it and benchmarked against a single fputs, to /dev/null so sink cost is excluded: 0.490 s vs 0.003 s over 200,000 calls on a 62-byte message -- 2.45 us against 0.02 us, AMPLIFICATION 161.2x, and that is a FLOOR because a real line-buffered console is worse. So a flood is not log noise; it is guest-controlled HOST-CPU amplification on a path -q cannot silence. (2) *** census_floods.py SAYS REACHABILITY 'NEEDS THE CALL GRAPH, AND A TOOL THAT GUESSED WOULD BE WORSE THAN ONE THAT DECLINES'. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE AND I WROTE IT. *** DEVICE_ACCESS() IS the dispatch entry memory_rw calls, so lexical containment inside its brace-matched body is a SOUND STRUCTURAL OVER-APPROXIMATION -- no call graph required. The seat built it: 776 fatal() under src/devices/ 475 inside a DEVICE_ACCESS() body (guest MMIO handler) 150 inside a switch default: in that body (unhandled-offset arm) 10 of those guarded by a latch in their OWN arm *** 140 UNLATCHED AT THE SITE, in 53 files *** POSITIVE CONTROLS BOTH LAND, and it resolves PER-PATH -- the resolution my census says it lacks. It flags dev_rtc.c:168-173 (the two pre-#429 arms this row names), and in dev_wdc.c it correctly SEPARATES :731/:761 (latched by warned_badlen, #337's work) from :583/:1007 (unlatched) -- i.e. it finds the path #337 MISSED inside a file my census scores as 'latched'. SO THE HONEST HEADLINE IS 140 SITES, NOT 543 CALLS AND NOT 72 FILES. Per-path, actionable, and mechanically re-derivable. (3) A RUNG-3 WITNESS IS AVAILABLE TODAY AT NEAR-ZERO COST, and the filing seat (me) missed it: regress/pit8253_latch_probe.py is committed and already drives real guest ARM instructions through real address decode to PA 0x7c000040-43 on an unmodified -E cats -- the 8253's own registers -- and dev_8253.c carries unlatched default:-arm fatal() at :158 and :184 (plus :250/:253). ONE MORE ARM on an already-committed probe witnesses an unsuppressable 161x-amplified flood. (4) DETECTOR, NOT FIX, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL: the round-scope rule takes ONE site, and a second only in the SAME DEVICE. rtcflood and wdcflood are different devices, so THE PROJECT'S OWN SCOPE RULE FORBIDS FIXING THIS CLASS IN ONE ROUND -- 140 sites at one round each is not a plan. Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** DO NOT DROP, DO NOT FIX AS WRITTEN -- THE FILED FIX IS PROVABLY INERT, AND THE REAL ITEM IS BIGGER. *** Two seats dropped this for being READ-only and the adjudicator overturned on mechanism; both were reasoning about the wrong fix. MEASURED (build/gxemul, -v -v -V -T -E cats -M 32): device order is 8259 @0x7c000020, 8259 @0x7c0000a0, *** 8253 @0x7c000040 ADDED AFTER BOTH PICs, *** pccmos @0x7c000070. The pointer copy sits at bus_isa.c:224-225, between the first device_add (:223) and the second (:235); the 8253's device_add is at :244. Construction order confirmed in the RUNNING PROGRAM, not inferred -- and it independently confirms the 0x7c000040 mapping. MEASURED (grep census): pending_timer_interrupts has exactly ONE writer (dev_8253.c:282) and TWO pointer-cachers (bus_isa.c:225, dev_v3.c:298), both caching before their 8253 can exist. *** MEASURED, AND THIS IS THE PART NOBODY STATED: dev_8253.c contains ZERO decrements of pending_interrupts_timer0. *** Every other timer device in the tree drains its own counter from inside its own DEVICE_ACCESS handler -- dev_jazz.c:423,443, dev_luna88k.c:800, dev_mc146818.c:563, dev_vr41xx.c:634, dev_footbridge.c:583,594-595. The 8253 ALONE outsourced its drain to bus_isa.c:134-138. READ: that drain is unreachable for TWO INDEPENDENT reasons, *** so moving the pointer copy after device_add -- the fix as filed -- changes NOTHING observable: *** (1) nothing ever calls isa_interrupt_deassert for line 0, as dev_8253.c has no INTERRUPT_DEASSERT; and (2) dev_8259.c clears irr DIRECTLY on EOI (:107, :122), bypassing the isa deassert handler entirely. REFILE AS: 'the 8253's pending-interrupt counter has no reachable drain -- it is the only timer device in the tree that cannot ack', grade DESIGN + needs-witness. Consequence (READ): once any guest touches the PIT, in_use goes 1, the counter rises monotonically and never drains, so DEVICE_TICK re-asserts isa.0 on EVERY device tick (TICK_SHIFT 14) rather than at the programmed rate. TWO THINGS THE FILING SEAT MISSED: dev_v3.c:298 is not merely 'the same shape' -- it is the same bug for the same reason needing the same two-part fix; and if a machine ever created two ISA buses (bus_pci.c calls bus_isa_init at :476 and :1060), the second copy would be NON-NULL AND ALIAS THE FIRST BUS'S 8253 -- worse than NULL, and silent. THE WITNESS THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, rung 3 on -E cats: program counter 0 to ~18 Hz, free-run 200 ms, read the 8259 IRR (expect bit0), write specific-EOI 0x60 to 0x7c000020, free-run ~5 ms, read IRR again. Draining correctly => 0 (next tick due at ~55 ms); no drain => 1 again on the very next device tick. Clean discriminator, no source change. — evidence: build/gxemul -E cats device order; grep census of the drain sites·······

Assessment (initial problem)✓2026-08-21 — CONFIRMED — [NOT A PANEL STAGE: SINGLE-SEAT RE-READ] This is a flagship RE-READ of the tree's only i8254 source during a batched regress pass, NOT a panel stage. It arrived on a row that had been FILED with one seat -- and a filing plus one re-read is counted by check_stage_panels as a two-of-nine STAGE, which reddened section H for a row nobody had convened a panel on. That is a real artefact worth naming: a batched pass that touches filed rows can promote a filing into a short stage without anyone deciding to. Annotated rather than silently left red, and the finding itself stands. STILL AN HONEST UNKNOWN after a flagship re-read of the tree's only source. _scratchpad/i8254.txt's latch section says the Counter Latch Command 'do[es] not affect the programmed Mode of the Counter in any way', and that between the two latched-byte reads 'read or write or programming operations of OTHER Counters may be inserted' -- nothing about the same counter's read pointer, either way. The reading cannot settle it from what is in the tree. — evidence: fable5 batched regress pass, 2026-08-21·✓2026-08-20 — UNKNOWN — RAISED BY CODEX as half of its DO-NOT-SHIP verdict on #440, and it is the half that survives scrutiny. If rd_msb is already 1 when the latch command arrives, the FIRST latched read has rw == MSB and #440 immediately clears the latch -- so only ONE byte has been read after the count was latched. *** A byte read BEFORE the latch command cannot be a byte of the newly latched value, *** which sits badly with p. 8's 'two bytes must be read'. On that reading R9 pins the implementation's assumption rather than the specification. THE MEASURING SEAT REACHED THE SAME FACT AND THE OPPOSITE READING: at odd parity the first read takes the byte the format calls for and unlatches, which it argues is CLOSER to hardware, and it measured the values (0x9c00 where #439 gave 0x0000). *** BOTH SEATS AGREE ON WHAT THEY CANNOT SETTLE: the local i8254 text does not say whether a Counter Latch Command rewinds the read flip-flop, and there is no other 8253/8254 source in the tree. *** So this is filed as an UNKNOWN and recorded in the source as one, rather than resolved 7-1. An honest UNKNOWN outranks a confident guess, and a majority has been wrong on mechanism in this project at least six times. Codex's proposed shape if it is ever settled against #440: track TWO POST-LATCH READS rather than reusing the format flip-flop -- a boolean `latched` is insufficient when the read phase can be MSB at latch time. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260820_183311/ (7/7 scriptable) + opus5 measuring seat······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — Found by the pass-2 measuring seat, and it is a fair hit on the round's own reasoning. PCR/RTCSR/RTCOR/RFCR all do `idata & mask` with NO byte_order term, so on big-endian a 4-byte access to them takes the LAST two bytes while BCR2/BCR3 now take the FIRST; and they PROMOTE a 1-byte write while BCR2/BCR3 now DROP it. The #441 comment cites them to justify servicing and then services differently on both axes. WHICH CONVENTION IS RIGHT IS NOT DECIDABLE HERE: there is no SH-4 document in this tree (sh4_manual.txt is ONE BYTE), so this is an honest UNKNOWN about the hardware and a real internal inconsistency about the model. One round takes one site, so #441 recorded the divergence in the source rather than silently unifying five registers on a guess. A related nit worth carrying: the round's claim that 'BCR1 already consults byte_order' is true but weak precedent -- BCR1 ORs in a strap bit, it does not place a lane. — evidence: pass-2 seat, read against dev_sh4.c·······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-21 — CONFIRMED — *** MEASURED, AND IT IS A SECOND INDEPENDENT RUNG-3 REPRODUCTION OF #442's DEFECT RATHER THAN A VARIANT OF IT. *** dev_footbridge.c never calls timer_remove() and never lowers the frequency on disable: :583 zeroes the counter ONCE on a control write and leaves the struct timer running at full rate. So the PRODUCER runs while the CONSUMER is blind. arm, DISABLE, free-run 4 s, re-enable, drain -> backlog 3051 arm, ENABLED, free-run 4 s, drain -> backlog 3051 (identical) THREE CONSEQUENCES, and the first is why #442 could not have been fixed the other way: 1. It defeats a CONSUMER-side bound entirely -- a mutant placing #442's clamp in DEVICE_TICK delivered ZERO ticks after a 46 s disabled interval, byte-for-byte the shipped defect. This is the measurement that turned the panel's unanimous Q1 answer from a preference into a proof. 2. *** A guest that disables and later re-enables gets an interrupt storm proportional to the disabled interval -- 2772 pending after 46 s EVEN WITH #442 SHIPPED. *** #442 bounds the counter per second of the timer's own rate; it does not stop a legitimately accrued second of debt arriving in one tick. 3. The SIGALRM catch-up cost is paid for a timer the guest turned off. Not folded into #442 under the reopening rule: same device, but a DIFFERENT semantic class (lifecycle of the timer object, not the bound on a counter) and no single fix design covers both -- #442 clamps, this needs the timer stopped or its rate dropped on disable, which is a behaviour change with its own oracle. — evidence: _scratchpad/fbpending_drain.py + the #442 pass-1 measuring seat·······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-21 — CONFIRMED — READ, found by the #442 pass-1 measuring seat while tracing the drain path. The arm that handles TIMER_x_CLEAR acts on the access without checking whether it was a read or a write, so a guest that merely READS the register performs the acknowledgement. That is a real fidelity defect and it is also a hazard for any DEBUGGER or probe that dumps the register window: a read-only inspection mutates device state. Note this project's own probes deliberately use guest loads rather than debugger `dump` precisely because dump does NOT route through device handlers -- so a probe reading this register through a guest load would silently drain the backlog it was trying to measure. Distinct semantic class from #442 (an access-direction guard, not a counter bound), so the reopening rule barred it from that round. — evidence: _scratchpad/fbpending_drain.py + the #442 pass-1 measuring seat·······

It read "A heap-buffer-overflow in arcbios.c set_env()" and THAT IS THE WRONG FILE AND THE WRONG FUNCTION. *** ASan reports the overflow at arcbios.c:2391 because that is where the READ happens, and the first filing -- mine -- followed the report there. set_env() is CORRECT CODE. Its append branch grows both arrays before writing to either, and its envstrings is malloc+memset at the call site. The buffer it is handed has no terminator, and *** A CALLEE CANNOT DETECT A MISSING TERMINATOR FROM THE INSIDE ***, so "harden the callee instead" is not a trade-off here, it is an impossibility. The owner is the caller, machine_sgi.c:100. My own pass-1 hypothesis -- that the linear search read out of bounds BEFORE the reported line -- was MEASURED FALSE: the search iterates over valid strdup'd names. MEASURED at the point of use: first_NUL_at = -1 on ip12/ip28/ip30/ip35 (no terminator anywhere in the 40 in-bounds bytes; they are ASan's 0xbe fill) and 17 on ip32. Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-21 — CONFIRMED — *** THE SHARPEST FORM OF A TRAP THIS PROJECT ALREADY RECORDS, AND IT REACHED THE TOP-LEVEL HARNESS INVOCATION. *** The full battery was started as bash run.sh 2>&1 | tail -45 in the background, and later killed. *** IT REPORTED EXIT CODE 0. *** A pipeline's status is the LAST command's, so the exit code belonged to `tail`, which succeeded in reading a truncated stream. Two things went wrong together and either alone would have been survivable: 1. THE VERDICT WAS FALSE -- a killed battery reported success. 2. THERE WAS NOTHING TO READ EITHER WAY. `| tail` buffers until the pipeline ends, so the output file sat at 0 BYTES for the whole run and was still 0 bytes afterwards. Mid-run progress was invisible and the post-mortem was empty. Same genus as `cmd | head` reporting head's status, which this project already writes down and which bit twice more the same day -- once hiding a compile failure, once mangling an object list through a `tr` inside nested quoting. What is NEW is the SCALE: this is not a check inside a gate, it is the invocation of the ENTIRE 16-GATE BATTERY. A SECOND TRAP RODE ALONG WITH IT, and it nearly did more damage: with the real output empty, the obvious place to look was the shared log directory -- which still held the PREVIOUS battery's verdicts. Those read `asan-machine-sweep: PASS (3 checks)` and `log-hygiene: PASS (38 checks)`, both plausible and both STALE (the current gates give 11 and 48). Reading them as this run's result would have been the 'a green row means nothing' class in its purest form, and the only thing that prevented it was the check counts having moved that day. THE FIX USED: run under `exec > /tmp/battery.log 2>&1` so output streams to a file and the exit status is run.sh's own. The re-run produced REGRESS_PASS across all 16 gates in 48 minutes, with progress readable throughout. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT MECHANICAL: a verdict is believable only if its log ends in a terminal token. nightly_check.sh already treats a MISSING or STALE verdict as failure -- the same reasoning one level in would refuse a verdict whose log carries no REGRESS_PASS/REGRESS_FAIL line, which is exactly what a killed run leaves behind. That is checkable and is the part worth building. — evidence: measured: the killed invocation's own exit code and its 0-byte output file·······

CONSEQUENCE FOR #450's record, stated there too: :751's mis-link hazard is a counterfactual PARTLY BECAUSE this bug prevents the walk from ever reaching a node whose parent pointer would exercise it. Fixing this row may make that site live -- the coupling runs one way, like ctorabortclass before it. HONEST LIMIT: layout arithmetic and one corroborating step constant, no execution. Research (fix proposals)·…2026-08-19 — *** THE BRIEF'S FRAMING WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE HALF IT GOT WRONG CHANGES WHAT SHOULD BE FIXED. *** Verdict FIX-not-document, but not for the reason I gave it. * 0xE7 WDCC_FLUSHCACHE is DEFINED at wdcreg.h:130 and NEVER REFERENCED in dev_wdc.c; 0xEA has no constant anywhere in src/. Both fall to wdc_command()'s default:, which sets WDCE_ABRT, emits an UNLATCHED fatal(), and -- the part that matters -- does NOT set d->int_assert. MEASURED offline against the shipping wdc_command(): 0xE7 -> err=0x04 irq=0 fatal=1, status 0x51 (DRDY|DSC|ERR), against the 0x10 RECAL control at err=0x00 irq=1. * NO REAL GUEST ISSUES IT, and the negative is WELL CONTROLLED. With an IDE disk attached and a full filesystem lifecycle (MAKEDEV, fdisk, disklabel, newfs 64 MB FFS, mount, write, sync, umount, halt -p) OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly: 0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0. No 0xE7, no 0xEA. * IT REFUTED ITS OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS rather than resting on it: 'the drive does not advertise FLUSH CACHE' was tested with TWO discriminating IDENTIFY variants (word 83=0x5000 and 0x7000). The guest DEMONSTRABLY READ the new IDENTIFY -- it began issuing 0xEF SET FEATURES, which it never did before -- and STILL never flushed. Why OpenBSD declines is an honest UNKNOWN: there is no OpenBSD source in this tree, and reconstructing wd_flushcache from memory is exactly the trap the SH-manual rule exists to prevent. * *** THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE ARM, NOT THE OPCODE: 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE hits the same default: on EVERY `halt -p`, measured 4 of 4 shutdown runs. *** ABRT to the guest, no interrupt, unlatched host warning, and the guest swallows it silently. So the IDE side has a reachable reproducible fall-through TODAY, and FLUSH CACHE is an unreached member of the same set. * THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. diskimage_sync() takes a struct diskimage *, but dev_wdc.c only ever holds (machine, id, type) -- and THERE IS NO EXPORTED (machine,id,type) -> struct lookup; every public function in diskimage.c open-codes the same 6-line walk. Needs a diskimage_sync_id() wrapper, a WDCC_FLUSHCACHE_EXT constant, and a case arm that also sets int_assert. Built privately: 0xE7/0xEA become err=0x00 irq=1 fatal=0 with trace F(data) S(data), matching the SCSI sibling. * DETECTOR BUILT, and it COMPILES AGAINST BOTH TREES because the rows pass a RAW OPCODE INTEGER rather than the WDCC_ constant -- deliberately sidestepping the exact trap diff_diskimage_sync.c's header records, where naming the new symbol made the pre-fix arm a SETUP result. 9 rows / 0 failed pre-fix; 8 of 9 flip post-fix. Needs only two extra stubs given the flags gate_offline.sh already passes. * SCOPE: all three files are byte-identical between est/ and GXEMUL-SEC/. And wdc is far from landisk-only -- bus_isa, bus_pci, dev_pcic, dev_ps2_spd, machine_arc.c:235, machine_landisk.c:87 and promemul/of.c all instantiate it, so ARC IS A SECOND ATA RIG THAT WAS NOT TESTED. Words 82-87 -- the COMMAND SET SUPPORTED / ENABLED block -- are left ZERO by the opening memset. A device that advertises no command sets and aborts a command it never claimed is not obviously wrong. On that reading idesync is a MISSING FEATURE, not a durability defect, and the 'correct' fix is a much larger IDENTIFY change that collides with diff_wdc_identify.c's explicit frozen-scope banner (#405/#407/#408/#410/#411). The negative control is stronger than claimed and still does not rescue the row: word 83 = 0x5000/0x7000 sets the validity marker plus the flush bits, the guest demonstrably read the new block, and it STILL never flushed. With words 82, 85 and 86 zero the block is internally inconsistent, which is a plausible reason a driver would decline -- but that is a HYPOTHESIS, and 'why OpenBSD declines' remains an honest UNKNOWN. The wrapper claim is CHECKED TRUE: diskimage.c open-codes the machine->first_diskimage walk TWELVE times (:113, 321, 340, 360, 385, 1558, 2120, 2130, 2149, 2177, 2198, 2310); a diskimage_sync_id() would be the thirteenth. Cost: a new public export, a new constant, two case arms and a detector that can only ever be construction-tested -- against a command NO GUEST IN THIS TREE ISSUES and which the model CORRECTLY DECLINES TO ADVERTISE. Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** LIVE VIA TWO OPCODES IN TWO ARMS, NOT ONE -- AND THE SECOND ARM IS ABSENT FROM THIS ROW. *** dev_wdc.c:572-579, the 'Unsupported commands, without warning' group, sets WDCE_ABRT and returns with NO interrupt and NO log: measured 0xF5 -> err=0x04, irq=0, fatal=0. *** AND 0xF5 SEC_FREEZE_LOCK IS ISSUED ON A PLAIN LANDISK BOOT WITH A DISK *** -- no halt, no install. So the row is reachable at rung 4 today. Credit where it belongs: agy, grok and kimi EACH found this arm from the packet; this seat confirmed it by execution and supplied the boot witness. The ledger did not contain it -- see [[ledgerboiler]] for why, which is the more important finding. BLAST RADIUS, which no seat had quantified: int_assert is a LEVEL, not an edge. dev_wdc_tick() re-asserts on EVERY tick while it is set and only a STATUS read clears it (:999-1000). Measured: HELD-LINE 0xe0 (abort), shipping : 0 asserts over 1000 ticks HELD-LINE 0x10 RECAL, shipping : 1001 asserts over 1000 ticks after ONE status read, 1000 more: +0 asserts, 1 deassert HELD-LINE 0xe0 (abort), POST-FIX : 1001 asserts over 1000 ticks <-- 0 -> 1001 *** NOT A NEW CLASS: *** RECAL already behaves exactly this way for every implemented opcode today, and the deassert is clean. Exposure is a guest that issues an unimplemented opcode fire-and-forget and never reads status. BLANKET IS RIGHT, and the file settles it without an ATA spec (there is none in this tree -- _scratchpad/ has ARM, IDT, MC88100, MIPS only, so no page numbers may be cited). There are FIVE WDCE_ABRT sites and THREE ALREADY ASSERT: :465-466 (no disk image), :473-474 (CDROM IDENTIFY), :514/:517 (SET_FEATURES unknown subcommand -- measured 0xEF -> err=0x04, irq=3). Only :578 and :582 do not. Opcode-specific gating is what CREATED the inconsistency. IMPLEMENTATION TRAP: WDCC_STANDBY_IMMED (wdcreg.h:138) and ATAPI_STANDBY_IMMEDIATE (:206) are BOTH 0xe0 -- writing both case labels is a duplicate-case compile error. SEVERITY, honestly: measured harm today is NIL. Zero unimplemented-command warnings on a disk boot, OpenBSD swallows the 0xF5 abort and reaches the prompt, and halt -p stops the machine anyway. This is fidelity for guests we do not have. — evidence: /tmp/opuswdc/probe.c dual-oracle harness; landisk boot with -d iR:·······

No device was added to reach it. — note: *** THE THREE-MEMBERED OPTION SET APPLIES DIRECTLY TO THIS ROW (carrier rule, minted 2026-08-25 from #463). *** #463 de-fatalised a device by framing the choice as KEEP the unlatched `fatal()` versus DELETE it, chose delete, and its own research stage then found the third member had been shipping in-tree the whole time: **`memory_rw.c:495-523` bounds a guest-drivable diagnostic to 8 emissions via `n_trunc_msgs`, because 'probing at the end of a device's mapped range is common and benign'.** The carrier already said 'a guest-drivable fatal() needs a latch and not a verbosity flag' -- standing rule, never consulted by that round's two-membered framing. **So before this row is worked: the option set is DELETE / DECLINE / DECLINE+BOUNDED-ANNOUNCE, and the first step is to grep the fork for the existing idiom rather than reason from first principles.** #463 also established that a bounded announce is not merely acceptable but RECOVERS the self-announcing property that de-fatalising destroys -- which for an unlatched flood is the whole point, since the flood and the announcement are the same channel. *** MEASURED 2026-08-25, AND THE ROW IS AIMED AT THE WRONG SITE. *** The opus5 seat built a `cp -a` copy at /tmp/gxwdc, verified freshness independently of MAKE_RC, and left GXEMUL-SEC untouched (verified by `git status --porcelain`: no src file modified). *** THE FLOOD IS CONFIRMED AND IS WORSE THAN THE TITLE SAYS: *** 20 stores produce 20 `fatal()` lines WITH and WITHOUT `-q` (0 `debug()` lines either way), and the OVER-READ site at 500 iterations produced 2000 lines / 158,449 bytes of host log (`regress/artifacts/wdcflood/witness_20260825/n3.out`, preserved off the volatile session scratchpad this row used to cite). *** CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-08-26: this sentence said "the read path", which points a reader at the non-8-bit READ guard. `n3.out` is 2000x "reading too much" -- the RING OVER-READ. Same numbers, wrong site named. The correction had already landed in the round block, the source comment and the gate comment while this field kept the false wording -- which is the corrections-land-in-CHANGELOG-only failure this ledger records having made twice before, now three times. It was found by a mechanical sweep for stale claims across all five records, not by reading. *** *** BUT `:583`, THE SITE THIS ROW NAMES, IS THE MORE GATED OF TWO FLOODS. *** It requires an attached IDE image (`:461-468` early-returns with a silenceable `debug()` otherwise) and yields ONE line per store. The unnamed sibling `wdc_get_inbuf` over-read at `:160` requires NOTHING -- landisk adds wdc unconditionally at machine_landisk.c:90 -- is on the READ path, and yields FOUR lines per single guest instruction (measured: mov.b/mov.w/mov.l x20 give 20/40/80). SIBLING CENSUS: ten `fatal()` in dev_wdc.c, FOUR latched by #337, SIX UNLATCHED -- :145, :160, :583, :607, :704, :1025. **Fixing :583 alone leaves the strictly worse :160 floodable at 4x with no precondition**, which is the project's recorded 'grep for its siblings' failure. SAFE TO ADD -- measured, fixed 25 s windows, same host and binary: no disk prompt_reached=1 instrs=2,852,727,965 iR: 64MB blank prompt_reached=1 instrs=1,879,394,907 no disk (2) prompt_reached=1 instrs=2,382,496,189 iR: 64MB (2) prompt_reached=1 instrs=1,711,379,982 Both reach the installer menu; wd0 attaches and is probed; gate_crossfamily.sh's SH7751R,42 token is unaffected; the installer waits rather than auto-installing. *** TWO TRAPS. (1) SYNTAX: `-d i:R:<path>` ABORTS *** (diskimage_add(): invalid prefix char -- the parser at diskimage.c:1700-1755 takes all prefix chars before a SINGLE colon). The correct form is `-d iR:<path>`. Getting this wrong is exactly the 'latently red for two commits' shape. *** (2) THE DISK CONFIG RETIRES 28-34% FEWER INSTRUCTIONS IN THE SAME WALL TIME. *** Harmless today only because drive_guest.py:84 sets "budget": 0 -- landisk deliberately has no instruction ceiling. But its own comment says a NINSTRS floor is FILED, and *** a floor derived from today's diskless boot and applied to a disked one is a false-FAIL waiting to happen. *** Also: the base image must be R:-prefixed or the guest writes the shared rig image, and the installer prompt has NO TRAILING NEWLINE, which is why the rig needs drive_guest.py's pty predicate rather than line-oriented matching. — evidence: landisk boots with and without -d iR:, 4 fixed-window runs·······

The regress review remains FABLE-ONLY and is held and queued below. — evidence: Fable adjudication docket, 2026-08-20✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** THE FACT THAT DECIDES WHAT THIS ROUND CAN HONESTLY DO: THERE IS NO RUNNING COUNT. *** Found while writing the design brief. d->counter[3] is WRITTEN only in the mode-write path and READ only in the counter-read path -- IT NEVER DECREMENTS. timer0_tick() increments pending_interrupts_timer0 and touches nothing else. The file's own header carries the author's TODO at line 35: '(Split counter[] into reset value and current value.)' So d->counter[] is the PROGRAMMED RELOAD VALUE, FROZEN. gxemul models the timer's RATE (timer_add / timer_update_frequency) and its INTERRUPTS, but never a counting register. WHY THAT REFRAMES THE FIX: OpenBSD's microtime() latches and reads the counter to INTERPOLATE SUB-TICK TIME. Reachability inherits pitlatch's: OpenBSD's microtime() issues the latch command (_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/i386/isa/clock.c:207-209), so the clobber happens on every call. NOT MEASURED -- no probe has yet shown the downstream effect of the corrupted RW format, and the honest grade is READ until one does. Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-23 — *** THE ROW SAYS 'NOT WITNESSED', AND A WITNESS IS BOTH CONSTRUCTIBLE AND ADMISSIBLE. *** The carrier's own rule is that 'no witness of either kind' is a CHECKABLE claim and must be checked rather than asserted -- dfreq's was measured false by building one in a single session -- so this is that check, done by READING (flagged as a reading, not a measurement; the tree was busy with #461's pre-fix run and a probe would have contended with it). THE OBSERVABLE ALREADY EXISTS: cpu_sh.c:168-173 registers `iprio_%x` as a readable setting for EVERY 0x20 slot in 0..0xfff, which includes `iprio_3e0` (IRQ15). The hardwired priority loop at cpu_sh.c:390 is `for (i = SH4_INTEVT_IRQ0; i <= SH4_INTEVT_IRQ14; i += 0x20)`, so slot 0x3e0 is never written and keeps 0 while 0x3c0 (IRQ14) gets 1. Two `print` commands on an unmodified machine separate the two. AND RUNG 2 IS THE RIGHT RUNG FOR IT, not a concession: the ladder licenses machine construction as a reproduction for 'defects in code construction itself executes (init-time)', naming the macppc heap OOB #23 as the exemplar. This IS init-time -- the loop populates the priority table at CPU init and the defect is a slot it never reaches. The ladder's warning about rung 2 is that registration proves presence not reachability, for ACCESS-PATH defects; this is not one. WHAT A RUNG-2 WITNESS WOULD NOT SETTLE, said plainly: it observes the priority TABLE, not delivery. It cannot show that an asserted line 15 is dropped -- for that the carrier's free-running shape is required (sr=0x40000000, vbr into RAM, `bra .` after the trigger, breakpoint at VBR+0x600), and driving a PCIC line needs a PCI device landing on line 15, since dev_sh4.c:2951-2967 registers the 16 lines as `<path>.pcic.<i>` for bus_pci_init's pciirq rather than as anything a guest store reaches directly. So the honest split is: the priority-0 STATE is witnessable at rung 2 today; the DROPPED-DELIVERY symptom is not, and the round should not claim it is. STALE CITATION CORRECTED: the row cites dev_sh4.c:2822-2836 for the wiring; that range is now the default arm's fatal()/exit block. The wiring is at :2951-2967.·······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-23 — *** WITNESS CONSTRUCTIBLE AT RUNG 3, and the MANUAL confirms the value is wrong. *** dev_sh4.c:2715-2720 is a bare latch -- `odata = d->cpg_frqcr` with no reset value written at init, so a guest reads back whatever DEVINIT's memset left, i.e. 0x0000. THE MANUAL, READ LOCALLY rather than taken from a search summary: _scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt:18607-18608 reads 'FRQCR is initialized only by a power-on reset via the RESET pin. The initial value of each bit is determined by the clock operating mode', and the bit table immediately below at :18610-18614 gives initial values CKOEN=1 (bit 11), PLL1EN=1 (bit 10), PLL2EN=1 (bit 9) with bits 15-12 = 0. So the reset value carries at least 0x0E00 and is NEVER 0x0000. The register table at :18476 marks the reset column 'Undefined*'; :18607 is the footnote that explains the asterisk, so 'undefined' means MODE-DEPENDENT, not zero -- a distinction that would have been easy to read the wrong way from the table alone. A guest reading FRQCR therefore sees both PLLs disabled and clock output disabled, the opposite of the reset state. WITNESS: one 16-bit guest load from 0xffc00000 on an unmodified SH-4 machine. HONEST LIMIT, the same shape as sh4pcic15's: the model has no clock-operating-mode concept, so a round must DECIDE what to present rather than read one value off the manual. The three bits above are mode-INDEPENDENT and settle the floor; IFC2 and the divider bits are not.·······

Final review (flagship adjudication)✓2026-08-23 — dev_sh4.c's `case SH4_CPG_FRQCR` models FRQCR as a plain store/load with no initialisation, so a guest reads 0x0000. SH7750 Hardware Manual Rev.7.00 Table 10.3 gives the legal initial values as H'0E1A / H'0E23 / H'0E13 / H'0E0A depending on clock mode. THIS IS THE HONEST LONG-RUN ANSWER TO sh4pclock: real hardware derives the peripheral clock from FRQCR and the mode pins, and a seat measured that the CPU:peripheral ratio in that table is only ever 4 or 6 -- calibrated against dreamcast, whose 200 MHz / 50 MHz = 4 is a legal mode this tree independently knows. A round here could make pclock DERIVED rather than assigned. Note the bound is not enough on its own: machine_hpcsh.c sets no emulated_hz at all, so the tree does not even claim a Jornada CPU clock to divide.········

EVERY WAIT IN THE DMA PATH IS TIME-BOUNDED, so a decline lands on a 7-second timeout -> BLK_STS_IOERR -> EIO. Degraded and bounded, NOT a hang: codex's and glm's central fear does not materialise. *** BUT IT FOUND THE MECHANISM NEITHER SIDE NAMED, AND THE FOUR-ROUND IDIOM WALKS STRAIGHT INTO IT. *** The DMA window's tail store runs after every aligned break. The SUCCESS arm sets `idata = 0` before breaking -- which is why a completed transfer polls idle -- and both exits die BEFORE the tail. So 'keep the diagnostic, drop exit(1)', the shape #447/#459/#460/#461 all used, lets the guest's trigger value 1 flow into dma_reg[6] and *** +0x18 READS BUSY FOREVER. *** For Linux that is a bounded HZ/2 tax per transfer; for a guest that waits the NetBSD way -- its own control-window waits are unbounded spins, fetched verbatim -- it is a real hang. Fix is one line per declined arm: `idata = 0` before break, mirroring the success arm. *** AND FIRING THE COMPLETION EVENT IS THE ACTIVELY HARMFUL OPTION, the opposite of what the brief asked about. *** gdrom_dma_interrupt clears gd.transfer UNCONDITIONALLY and checks no error bit anywhere, so firing SYSASIC_EVENT_GDROM_DMA on an empty transfer exits the wait with BLK_STS_OK -- the block layer is told the read succeeded when zero bytes moved, and the guest consumes whatever was in the destination page AS DISK DATA. That is #460's invented-behaviour class reproduced at the block layer. The driver has exactly one error channel, the timeout, so 7-second EIO is not a compromise but the only honest signal available. IT ALSO STRENGTHENED THE ROUND'S WARRANT: :804 is a COMPLIANT-GUEST path today. gdrom_readdisk_dma writes the four DMA registers before sending packet 0x30; if diskimage_access fails on a short image, or OB-20's sector clamp rejects the request, handle_command leaves d->data == NULL and Linux -- told nothing it checks -- byte-writes 1 to +0x18. Measured 2026-08-25 on the #463 records audit. *** `codex` STREAMS its reasoning, so its file grows continuously and was 311 KB while still working. `grok` streams slowly -- 229 then 357 bytes, each sample a partial sentence. **`agy` writes NOTHING until it finishes**: its file sat at EXACTLY 0 bytes for minutes with a live `agy.exe` (pid 23548), then lands in one shot -- 8,044 bytes on the pass-2 panel. So for agy, and ONLY for agy, a zero-byte file is the normal mid-run state, and it is indistinguishable BY SIZE from the plain-`&` failure the carrier records (where a killed child leaves a zero-byte log). **The discriminator is the PROCESS, not the file**: `tasklist | grep agy` settles it in one command. Note the related trap already recorded -- check `tasklist` WITHOUT `/v`, because `/v` changes the column layout and a follow-up check using it once reported no processes when three were alive, nearly destroying a true positive. *** AND THE THIRD DEFECT IS IN THE FIX: A WALL-KEYWORD CHECK PRODUCES A FALSE POSITIVE ON ANY SEAT THAT READS THIS LEDGER. Measured 2026-08-25. *** After widening the seat check to catch the quota/403/429/stalled family, it scored a LIVE codex seat as WALLED. The seat was mid-answer at 225 KB and still running; what the check matched was **this project's own prose about walls** -- the rows describing a 403 mislabelled as 429, and the empty-response class -- echoed back by a seat that had been asked to read the ledger. **A keyword detector applied to a document ABOUT that keyword cannot work**, and the tasks most likely to trip it are exactly the records and matrix audits this project now runs routinely. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS POSITION AND TERMINATION, not presence -- which is what the carrier already says (`verify the CONTENT, never the size`) applied one level down: a walled seat's notice is the LAST thing in the file with nothing substantive after it, and the answer either ends mid-sentence or is the echoed brief. A live seat mentions a wall in the middle of a large body of its own reasoning and keeps going. `seat_verdicts.py` already uses a POSITION discriminator for exactly this reason; the seat check should borrow it rather than grep the whole tail. Cheapest interim guard, and it costs one line: **if the process is still alive, it is not walled** -- `tasklist` settles it, and this project has now used that test twice in one session (once to prove a 0-byte agy file was buffering rather than dead). *** SECOND MEASURED INSTANCE 2026-08-25 (`panel_20260825_112845`), AND THE SECOND DEFECT IS WORSE THAN THIS ROW SAYS -- IT IS NOT A TALLY PROBLEM, IT IS A LOST SEAT. *** Defect (1) reproduced exactly: the kimi CLI returned `provider.auth_error: 403 You've reached your usage limit for this billing cycle` and SEATS.txt printed `*** RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)`. Same wrong status code, same blurring of the wall-versus-transport line the carrier draws. *** BUT DEFECT (2) IS NOT MERELY AN UNDERCOUNT. *** This row records that the tally omits a substitute transport that ANSWERED. Measured today: `panel.sh` **never fires the substitute at all**. It launches exactly one kimi seat -- the CLI, at `:222` -- and its three Ollama seats are hardcoded to `$OLLAMA1/2/3` (glm, deepseek, minimax) at `:270/:274/:278`. Meanwhile `curl -s localhost:11434/api/tags` lists **`kimi-k3:cloud` as LIVE**, and three earlier panels (`panel_20260824_191634`, `panel_20260824_231824`, `panel_20260825_000248`) each hold an `ollama_kimi.txt`, so the seat was being fired BY HAND and then stopped being. *** SO THE HONEST STATUS OF THIS SEAT IS NOT "DOWN". *** kimi's CLI transport is walled; kimi itself is reachable and idle. Every panel since the CLI wall has silently run one seat short while a working transport sat unused -- which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape with an extra step, because here the roster does not even record a failure to investigate. RECOVERED IMMEDIATELY: the seat was fired by hand onto the live `wdcflood` pass-1 panel dir as `ollama_kimi.txt`. FIX OWED IN panel.sh, deliberately NOT APPLIED YET because panel.sh was RUNNING when this was found and bash reads a script incrementally -- editing a running script is its own defect class. The fix: fire `kimi-k3:cloud` as a fourth Ollama seat, and have the seat check report the CLI wall and the substitute SEPARATELY so a walled transport with a live substitute reads as one seat answered, not as a loss. Also correct `429` to the actual status text rather than a hardcoded code. *** AND THE GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS: WHEN A SEAT WALLS, ASK WHETHER THE MODEL IS REACHABLE BY ANOTHER TRANSPORT BEFORE RECORDING IT DOWN. *** The carrier already separates a wall from a refused connection; this is the third class -- **one transport walled, another live** -- and it is the only one where the seat is available the whole time and nobody asks.open

seatthinkburnseatthinkburn a FIFTH seat-failure class: an empty response wrapped in 260 KB of thinking, which every size check scores as the panel's best answerseatthinkburn a FIFTH seat-failure class: an empty response wrapped in 260 KB of thinking, which every size check scores as the panel's best answer — witness: measured -- _scratchpad/panel_20260825_024101_audit/consistency_deepseek-v4-pro_cloud.txt — note: MEASURED 2026-08-25 on the #463 consistency audit. `deepseek-v4-pro:cloud` returned **`"response": ""` -- completely empty -- inside a 265,845-byte JSON object whose `thinking` field is 260,678 bytes, with `done_reason: 'length'` and `eval_count: 65536`. It spent its ENTIRE output budget on hidden reasoning and never emitted an answer. *** IT IS DISTINCT FROM ALL FOUR RECORDED CLASSES. *** Not a WALL (no quota text, no 403/429). Not the ECHO-ONLY shape (it echoes nothing). Not a REFUSED CONNECTION (the daemon served it fine, for 267 seconds). Not the shared-transport outage (the other three cloud seats answered normally in the same firing). *** AND IT DEFEATS EVERY SIZE-BASED CHECK IN THE WORST DIRECTION: at 265 KB it is the LARGEST file in its panel and would be scored the best answer. *** The carrier already warns 'verify the CONTENT, never the size; the failure mode is a big file' -- this is that lesson in a new variant, where the bulk is not an echoed brief but the model's own reasoning. **It was diagnosable only by accident**: `panel_ollama.py` does `body = resp.get('response') or json.dumps(resp)`, so an empty response falls back to dumping the raw JSON. Had it written the empty string, the file would have been 0 bytes and indistinguishable from a transport failure. That fallback should be made deliberate, and documented as the thing that preserves the diagnosis. THE FIX, and it is cheap: the seat check must parse any Ollama output that starts with `{`, and report SEAT DOWN when `response` is empty -- naming `done_reason` and `eval_count`, because `length` says 'budget exhausted' while `stop` would say something else entirely. A working checker exists (used to produce this row) and needs wiring into `panel.sh` and `seat_verdicts.py`. CONTRIBUTING CAUSE worth recording separately: the brief was the ENTIRE 18 KB round-block draft. The carrier's rule is to INLINE every fact for packet-fed seats, and that rule is sound -- but inlining an 18 KB artifact and asking for exhaustive cross-checking gives a thinking model enough to reason itself past its own budget. **Inline the facts; do not inline an entire document and ask for an audit of it.** *** AND A SIXTH CLASS, MEASURED THE SAME SESSION on the matrix-review panel: THE SEAT'S OWN TRANSPORT DIED MID-ANSWER. *** `agy` returned 293 bytes reading `I have launched the topic cluster analysis script ... Waiting for background script completion.` followed by `Error: the connection to the agent was interrupted before the response finished: subscriber fell behind updates, stalled for 6s`. It is none of the five: no quota text (not a wall), it connected and worked for minutes (not a refused connection), it echoed nothing, it emitted a real partial answer rather than an empty response inside vast thinking, and the other seats on the same panel were unaffected (not the shared-Agent-tool outage). **The distinguishing shape: the seat DELEGATED to a background script and its own streaming connection dropped while it waited.** Two consequences. (1) The keyword set every seat check in this project uses -- quota / rate limit / balance / 403 / 429 / refused -- does NOT contain `interrupted`, `stalled`, or `subscriber fell behind`, so this scored as `answered`. Widened. (2) **It is worth RE-FIRING, unlike a wall**: a wall is the provider refusing and you wait it out; this is a dropped connection and the work simply did not survive. The re-fire rule the carrier already states for walled seats applies here with better odds. *** THE CONTRIBUTING CAUSE THIS ROW FILED WAS MEASURED FALSE THE SAME SESSION. *** It said the trigger was inlining an entire 18 KB document and asking for an exhaustive audit of it, and prescribed 'inline the facts; do not inline a document'. **A SECOND burn then happened on a brief a fraction of that size** -- 11 ledger rows, truncated narratives, ~10 KB -- with the identical signature: `response: ""`, `done_reason: 'length'`, `eval_count: 65536`, and 275,778 bytes of `thinking`. Larger thinking than the first burn, on a much smaller brief. **So SIZE IS NOT THE CAUSE**, and the prescription derived from it was wrong. What the two share is the TASK SHAPE, not the input size: both asked for an EXHAUSTIVE PER-ITEM AUDIT with several independent sub-questions per item (four categories over a document; four questions over each of eleven rows). The seat answered a 6.5 KB pass-2 REVIEW brief normally in the same session -- one subject, one set of questions. **The working hypothesis is now COMBINATORIAL: N items x M orthogonal questions, where the seat appears to explore the cross-product before emitting anything.** That is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and it is recorded as such -- the honest state is that the cause is NOT ESTABLISHED and the first stated cause is REFUTED. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which does not depend on the cause: **deepseek is unreliable for per-item audit tasks and reliable for single-subject review**, so route it accordingly rather than by brief size. And the detection rule is unchanged and now doubly warranted: parse the JSON, report SEAT DOWN on an empty `response`, and never score by file size -- both burns produced the LARGEST file in their panel. *** AND THE TEST THAT LOOKED LIKE A CONFIRMATION IS CONFOUNDED -- CORRECTED IMMEDIATELY RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING. *** deepseek ANSWERED a #463 research-stage brief cleanly (1,724 bytes, a real dissent) after burning on two audits, and that was momentarily reported as confirming the task-shape hypothesis over the size hypothesis. **It confirms nothing.** The brief was 3,614 bytes -- SMALLER than both that burned it (19,395 and 10,408) -- so it varies BOTH suspected causes at once and cannot discriminate between them. The honest state of the evidence: burns at 19,395 (per-item audit) and 10,408 (per-item audit); clean answers at 8,583 (single-subject review) and 3,614 (single-subject research). **Size and shape are perfectly correlated across all four data points**, so nothing here separates them. A discriminating test exists and is cheap -- a LARGE single-subject brief, or a SMALL per-item one -- and until someone runs it the cause remains NOT ESTABLISHED. *Recorded because the first stated cause was already refuted once; a second unearned cause would be the same defect with better manners.*open

scoreclaimhexscoreclaimhex check_score_claims reads a slash-separated HEX LIST as a score claim, and reports a stale score that was never writtenscoreclaimhex check_score_claims reads a slash-separated HEX LIST as a score claim, and reports a stale score that was never written — witness: measured -- _scratchpad/precommit_463.log, section U, three FAIL lines — note: MEASURED 2026-08-25 during #463's pre-commit. Section U reported THREE stale score claims in `asic_badaddr_probe.py`'s docstring -- `claims 00/0`, `10/0`, `20/0`, pin is 12. **None of them was ever written.** All three come from ONE line of ordinary prose: `bases 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, a slash-separated list of hex group bases. The pattern `(?<![\d/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])` sees `0x00/0x10` and takes `00` / `0`. *** IT IS A FALSE FAIL, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE FAILURE FROM THE ONE SECTION U EXISTS TO CATCH, AND IS STILL EXPENSIVE. *** A gate that reddens on prose trains its reader to explain away red rows, which is exactly how a REAL stale score would then get waved through. And this project writes `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30` constantly -- the fourth-word invariant is naturally expressed that way -- so it will recur in any file section U checks. WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, and deliberately: #463 reworded its own docstring to use commas, because the round's material is unshipped (L1) while `check_score_claims.py` is a shared gate and editing it is a different scope. **The workaround is also the weaker fix** -- it relies on every future author avoiding a natural notation. THE REAL FIX is one lookbehind: reject a match whose left digit run is preceded by `0x` or `0X`, i.e. require the numerator not be part of a hex literal. Note the existing escape hatch (`write '<N>-row' on the same line`) does NOT help here, because the denominator the checker invented is 0 and nobody would write `0-row`.open
