ledgerstateliesledgerstatelies the ledger's schema had NO WRITTEN SEMANTICS for `state`, so two seats read opposite conventions into one string and five agreed on 4 of 11 rowsledgerstatelies the ledger's schema had NO WRITTEN SEMANTICS for `state`, so two seats read opposite conventions into one string and five agreed on 4 of 11 rows — HOLD: THIS IS ITS OWN ROUND. The matrix panel below is its PASS-1. Adjudicated 2026-08-25: #463 may not repair it -- ~50 instances across five classes is a records-correction round, and the standing rule for those (budget a SECOND review pass, because corrections repeat the errors they correct) cannot be honoured inside another round. — witness: none needed -- the ledger is the artifact; every finding cites a row id — note: PASS-1 PANEL: `_scratchpad/panel_20260825_030653_matrix`. SIX SEATS FIRED, FIVE ANSWERED, ONE DOWN. grok, codex, minimax-m3, kimi-k3:cloud and glm-5.2 answered; **agy FAILED on a SIXTH seat-failure class -- its own streaming transport dropped mid-answer** (`connection to the agent was interrupted ... subscriber fell behind updates, stalled for 6s`) -- and was re-fired, since a dropped connection is worth retrying where a wall is not. *** grok's verdict is the headline: DO NOT TRUST STATES. *** THE FINDINGS, by class. (1) STATE CONTRADICTS SUBSTANCE: `pitlatch` and `pitclobber` sit `in work` while every closure note says CLOSE and the residual their hold names is already discharged by a CLOSED carrier; `hpcshcpu` is `open` while its own note says DROP FROM THE ACTIONABLE QUEUE; `m8invpred` is `held` behind a codex wall discharged 2026-08-20; `reprowitness` is `in work` although the witness ladder it produced has been in the carrier since 2026-08-19; `gdromdmawidth` is `open` while admitting shipped code carries a comment under its name. (2) *** THE BURIAL SHAPE, TEXTBOOK FORM: `b115` and `b126` EACH CARRY TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS UNDER ONE ID. *** Closing either on one defect buries the other -- the exact hazard the carrier records. This is the highest-severity finding here. (3) STALE BLOCKERS: `gdromdmawidth` waits on `sh4gdromexit`, a carrier that will never do the work attributed to it. (4) UNEVIDENCED CLOSES: `rtcdet`, `gdromdmadefault`, `witnessinvisible` close asserting shipped substance with no commits; `b75` is a contested close with no recorded adjudication; `fbwitness` closes with an absent witness while its title claims a probe. (5) A CORRECTION THAT DID NOT PROPAGATE: a measured 4x inflation was corrected in `arcbiosubsan` and never in `sgiarcbiosoob`, which still asserts it -- mechanical rule 2 (grep for a claim's SIBLINGS before calling it fixed) failing in the ledger itself. *** AND A WARNING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS ROUND, because the round that filed it got this wrong THREE TIMES: THE LEDGER HAS MULTIPLE SCHEMA ERAS AND A CHECKER THAT KNOWS ONE ERA INVENTS ANOMALIES. *** (a) Narrative lives in `entries` on 198 older rows and `state_note` on 19 newer ones; counting only the latter reported 191 rows with no narrative when the true number is ZERO. (b) `witness` is FORWARD-ONLY from 2026-08-19 (`CLAUDE.md:1191`), so of 16 closed-without-witness rows FOURTEEN are compliant and only `rtcdet` and `fbwitness` are owed. (c) `closure.by` postdates part of the ledger. (d) 'open/held WITH commits' looked like 16 anomalies and is ZERO -- all sixteen carry a HOLD marker, which is the normal batching state by design. **Establish the validity rule for each class BEFORE touching a cell, and print a denominator beside every count.** *** THE SCOPE WAS MEASURED AND IT IS 12 ROWS, NOT ~50. The ~50 figure this row was FILED with was my own, and it was wrong for the FIFTH time in one session, by the same mechanism every previous time. *** Establishing each class's validity rule BEFORE counting -- which is what the adjudication demanded -- collapses the raw counts hard: A closed-without-witness 16 raw -> **2** (14 predate the 2026-08-19 forward-only cutoff and are COMPLIANT); B closed-without-commits 6 raw -> **3** (three are withdrawn / not-a-bug / documented-only); C open-or-held-with-commits 17 raw -> **1** (fifteen carry a HOLD, the normal batching state, and one was `asicbadaddr` itself, closed when #463 committed); D closed-without-closure.by 2 raw -> **2**; E state-contradicts-closure 30 raw -> **5**. *** RULE 5, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COST THE MOST: `closure.note` MAY DISPOSE OF A STAGE, NOT THE ROW. *** The ledger defines four `phase_labels` -- assess, research, review, regress -- so `CLOSE (assess)` closes the ASSESS STAGE and the row legitimately stays `held`. TWENTY-FIVE of class E's thirty are that shape; `exitsweep`'s own hold says so out loud (*"CLOSURE REVERTED ... the fable5 batch answered this row's held stage"*). Reading a stage-scoped disposition as a row-scoped one manufactured 25 false defects. THE TWELVE THAT SURVIVE: rtcdet, fbwitness, gdromdmadefault, witnessinvisible, gdromdmawidth, gate3scope, m437ord, m8invpred, ledgerwitness, cmtattr, hpcshcpu -- plus this row. Note the convergence worth trusting: `fbwitness`, `rtcdet`, `gdromdmadefault` and `witnessinvisible` were named INDEPENDENTLY by the reading seats AND fall out of the mechanical census, which is the only kind of agreement that counts here. RECONCILIATION, demanded by the adjudicator before either number may be quoted: the class column sums to **13 instances** and the repair set is **11 rows**. 13 - 1 dedup (`fbwitness` is in BOTH closed-no-witness and closed-no-commits) - 1 self (`ledgerstatelies` is this tracking row) = 11. Both numbers are correct; the arithmetic was simply never shown, which made the correction READ as contradicting its own column -- **a sixth counting defect sitting inside the correction that reports the fifth.** *** THE ROUND'S CENTRAL FINDING, MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT WHAT EITHER SEAT CLAIMED: `state` IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE RECORD. *** Two file-reading seats disagreed on `fbwitness` -- one said `CLOSE (assess)` disposes of a STAGE so the row must be `held`, the other said it retires the assessment so `closed` is fine. Settled empirically rather than by vote, and BOTH inferences are unsupported: **23 rows carry the IDENTICAL `closure.note` of `CLOSE (assess)` and they are spread across THREE states -- 12 `held`, 7 `in work`, 4 `closed`** (the closed four being ns16550, fablequeue, carrier, fbwitness). The obvious second hypothesis was tested and also fails: the number of STAGES with recorded entries is statistically identical across the three groups (mean 1.8 / 1.8 / 1.9, same min and max), so stage coverage does not explain the split either. **`state` and `closure.note` are independent fields with no enforced relationship**, so a reader cannot derive one from the other and neither can a checker. That is why 'DO NOT TRUST STATES' is the correct verdict, and it reframes this round: **the repair cannot be a mechanical rewrite of 11 cells, because there is no rule to rewrite them TO.** The round must first establish what `state` MEANS -- most plausibly 'is there work outstanding on this row', which is a different question from 'has any stage been adjudicated' -- and only then repair. ALSO REFUTED HERE, and worth keeping because it was checkable in two minutes: the claim that `fbwitness` is ALONE among its 2026-08-20 cohort in being closed. That cohort is 84 rows -- 17 closed, 43 held, 11 dropped, 13 in work -- and four of the closed share `fbwitness`'s exact closure string. A seat's argument from 'this row is the only one' is worth checking every time; this one was wrong. *** FIVE SEATS, ELEVEN ROWS, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE NOISE. *** agy, kimi-k3, glm-5.2, minimax-m3 and grok each assigned a correct state to all eleven rows, reading the same ledger under the same four validity rules stated in the brief. **They agree on only 4 of 11.** `hpcshcpu` drew THREE different answers (closed / dropped / held); six more drew two. This is what a field with no derivable meaning looks like from the outside: competent independent readers do not converge, because there is nothing to converge ON. *** IT ALSO PARTITIONS THE ROUND CLEANLY, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. *** **UNANIMOUS (4) -- and all four are ALREADY IN THE RIGHT STATE**: `gdromdmadefault` and `witnessinvisible` (closed, missing `commits`), `m437ord` (closed, missing `closure.by`), `cmtattr` (held, correct as-is). What these need is FIELDS, not state changes, and a field that is absent is absent under any definition of `state` -- so they are repairable NOW, independently of the rule question. **SPLIT (7)**: rtcdet, fbwitness, gdromdmawidth, gate3scope, m8invpred, ledgerwitness, hpcshcpu. Every one of these turns on what `state` MEANS, and none can be repaired until that is settled -- editing them now would be manufacturing the appearance of correctness by picking whichever seat I found most persuasive. **THE SPLIT IS ALSO A CHECK ON THE 23-ROW FINDING**, arrived at from the opposite direction: that one measured one closure string against three states; this one measures five readers against one row set. Both say the same thing and neither depends on the other's method. *** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-25, AND IT REFRAMED THE ROUND WHILE CONVICTING ME OF ONE OVERREACH. *** The ruling: `state` and `closure.note` are different TENSES. The note is a PAST-TENSE event log of what happened to a STAGE; `state` is a PRESENT-TENSE assertion of what the ROW still OWES. **Under that reading the multi-state spread of one closure string is the ledger WORKING AS DESIGNED, not the defect** -- rows that experienced the same stage event legitimately differ in what else they owe -- and the stage-coverage test failing is CORROBORATION rather than a second mystery, because state depends on what REMAINS, not on how much happened. **SO THE THING TO FILE IS THE MISSING SCHEMA SEMANTICS, NOT THE SPREAD.** That single absence is the cause behind six mis-counts in one session, two seats inferring opposite conventions from one string, and five seats agreeing on only 4 of 11 rows. The fix is written: a `state_semantics` block now sits in the ledger's own schema, PENDING OWNER RATIFICATION, forward-only in the same way `witness` was. *** MY OVERREACH, RETRACTED IN PLACE: I wrote that 'for most of the 11 there is no fact of the matter to restore -- only a decision'. THAT IS FALSE AND IT WAS CONVENIENT FOR ME*** -- it converts eleven tedious substance reads into one interesting rule question. What died was a repair METHOD (derive state from the note), not the fact of the matter, which is read from commits, gates, holds and filed questions -- exactly how `asicbadaddr` was closed, with no note convention needed. **The seminar is over in one paragraph; the eleven reads remain owed.** *** AND NO NUMBER IN THIS ROW MAY BE QUOTED AS A PREMISE UNTIL A SECOND PARTY CHECKS IT. *** I have mis-counted this ledger six times in one session. Every ruling above depends on the EXISTENCE of the spread, not its size -- ONE held row and ONE closed row sharing a closure string already prove non-derivability -- so the whole second-party check is two greps. The figures 23, 84 and the 1.8/1.8/1.9 stage means are UNVERIFIED SUPPORTING COLOUR, labelled as such, and are leads rather than premises. *** A SEVENTH COUNTING HAZARD, FOUND BY MAKING IT: SEAT NAMES ARE NOT SEAT ANSWERS. *** While closing #463's stages I reported research at 9/9; it was 8/9. The `codex` entry on that stage is a **`[HELD AWAITING SEAT:` MARKER** -- a record that the seat is OUTSTANDING -- and I counted it because I counted seat NAMES. `check_stage_panels.py` excludes marker entries deliberately, and its own comment says exactly why: *'otherwise marking a gap would close it.'* **Writing down that a seat is missing would, under a name-count, make the stage look complete** -- the seat-failure-as-agreement shape in its purest mechanical form. **THE LEDGER CARRIES 44 SUCH MARKER ENTRIES**, each one a seat that has NOT answered. Any future census of panel coverage that counts names rather than answers over-reports by up to that much. Three marker tokens exist and all three must be excluded: `[HELD AWAITING SEAT:`, `[NOT A PANEL STAGE: SINGLE-SEAT RE-READ]`, and `[RUN UNDER THE PRE-2026-08-16 POLICY]`. *This belongs with the schema-semantics finding rather than beside it: `entries` is not a list of answers, it is a list of EVENTS, and some events record an absence. That is the same present-tense/past-tense confusion that `state` and `closure.note` embody, one level down.* *** A NEW INSTANCE OF THIS ROW'S OWN DEFECT, FOUND 2026-08-25 BY THE ADJUDICATOR TRIPPING OVER IT WHILE ADJUDICATING THIS VERY BLOCK. *** Asked to rule on the queue, the fable5 seat reported that `idesync` "is already closed as document-do-not-fix". The ledger says `state = "in work"` with `commits` EMPTY. Both readings are half right, and the shape is new: *** THE DISPOSITION IS SETTLED BUT THE DOCUMENT HAS NOT SHIPPED. *** The row carries an opus5 REVIEW verdict (2026-08-20) of DOCUMENT-DO-NOT-FIX on a deciding fact nobody else raised -- the drive never advertises FLUSH CACHE, so the highest IDENTIFY word written never sets it -- plus a closed assess stage (`closure.by = fable5`, `CLOSE (assess)`). A SUBSTANCE reader therefore sees a finished decision and says "closed"; a STATE reader sees no commits and says "unfinished". Under the semantics now written, `closed` means discharged BY WORK, and a documenting commit IS work that has not happened -- so the state field is RIGHT and the adjudicator was WRONG, while the adjudicator was right about the only thing anyone would act on. *** THE LESSON IS THAT `document-do-not-fix` NEEDS ITS OWN DISCHARGE, AND NOTHING TRACKS IT. *** A row in this state is invisible to both readings: it looks decided to anyone reading the verdict and claimed to anyone reading the state, so nobody ships the document. That is an UNDISCHARGED OBLIGATION with no carrier -- the class section I of precommit exists for, one field over. Candidate fix, NOT applied pending ratification: `closed` requires either a commit or an explicit `documented-only` closure badge, so an assessed-not-changed record cannot close without the record existing. The project's ethos already demands honest 'assessed, not changed' records; what is missing is anything that NOTICES when one was promised and never written.open

It is also outside the depends-on enumeration (it edits a DEFINITION -- the array bound -- and definitions are never inside), and outside even the corrected contract, which claims the bound on `r`, not the bound on the arrays. With the detector shipped, L1 is unavailable. **"Built and works" was never a license**, and every shipped row enlarges the re-measure surface of every future kill table -- measured repeatedly in this project. THE CLOSING ROW, ready to lift: `m13w2x11w0` writes +0x18 and +0x20 and reads back +0x18, wanting 0xc3; under the shrink it reads 0xd4. It would additionally pin `case 0x20:`, one of the five labels the probe header lists as pinned by nothing. THE GENERAL GAP, which is larger than this mutant: **the detector verifies the INDEX and never the ARRAY it indexes into.** The whole invariant is 'r indexes uint32_t[3]', and the [3] half is asserted by the struct declaration alone, which no row reads. Disclosed as out-of-contract in the probe docstring (honesty clause iii). Related: `asicarray4` proposes padding the arrays to [4], which would change what this mutant even means.open

citestalecitestale a same-file line citation is invalidated by the round's OWN later edits -- six instances in one round, and no gate checks itcitestale a same-file line citation is invalidated by the round's OWN later edits -- six instances in one round, and no gate checks it — witness: measured -- six instances in #463 alone, each caught by a seat or by re-reading, never by a gate — note: The carrier already states the rule (*'a line number in a comment is invalidated by your own edits to that file; re-grep every same-file citation AFTER the last edit'*). **#463 broke it SIX TIMES while knowing it**, which is the argument for mechanising rather than restating: (1) `:200,:203` for the debug() calls, stale when the #463 comment was first inserted; (2) the SAME cite stale AGAIN after the comment was trimmed three lines shorter -- **a correction that went stale a second time**; (3) `:230` for `default:` in the round block, found by a records-audit seat; (4) `:144-152` for the mask_13 handler in the probe docstring; (5) four BARE artifact names with seven candidates each -- citation decay by NAMESPACE rather than by movement, caught by section X; (6) `:227` for `default:` going stale inside the very edit that corrected a different overstatement. *** THE SHAPE IS ALWAYS THE SAME AND ALWAYS INVISIBLE: the text does not change and stops being true. *** Section D checks that ADDED citations EXIST; it cannot see a citation that still resolves to a line of the wrong content, and existence is not correctness -- its own output says so. PROPOSED CHECK, cheap and mechanical: for each `:NNN` in a source comment, require an adjacent ANCHOR TOKEN (a short quoted fragment of the cited line) and verify the token is actually ON line NNN. That converts every citation into a self-verifying pair and catches movement, trimming and namespace decay alike. Cost: one token per citation, and the round that wrote six stale ones would have caught all six at commit time. *** A SEVENTH INSTANCE, AND IT PRODUCED A BETTER FIX THAN THE CHECKER THIS ROW PROPOSED. *** Adding seven lines about transaction closure moved `default:` again, and `:229` came to point at `d->mask_9[r] = idata;`. Caught only because the citation was re-derived immediately after the edit -- the manual discipline works exactly as long as someone remembers it, which is the definition of a check that eventually does not happen. **THE REAL FIX IS CHEAPER THAN AN ANCHOR-TOKEN CHECKER: a SAME-FILE citation does not need a line number.** `default:` is in the same function, below the comment; `the default: arm below` and `the struct above` are unambiguous, need no maintenance, and CANNOT DECAY -- there is nothing there to go stale. Applied: all same-file `:NNN` citations in this comment are now positional, and the only numbers left are CROSS-FILE -- and the ENUMERATION here named four when there are SIX (`core/debugmsg.c:375`, `core/debugmsg.c:384-390`, `cpu_sh_instr.c:790-798`, `dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:72`, `dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:74`, `configure:312-314`); the CLAIM that all remaining are cross-file is true and zero bare `:NNN` remain, but the list was not exhaustive -- which edits to THIS file cannot move. **THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT: cite a line number only ACROSS files; within a file, cite by POSITION or by the name of the thing.** That removes the entire class from same-file comments at zero cost, and leaves the checker worth building for the cross-file remainder, which is a much smaller surface -- seven instances this round were ALL same-file. *** AN EIGHTH INSTANCE, AND THIS ONE REFUTES A JUDGEMENT RATHER THAN AN EDIT. *** After converting every same-file citation to a positional reference, two bare cross-file numbers remained, each following a QUALIFIED cite to the same file. I inspected them and judged the idiom clear enough -- `core/debugmsg.c:384-390, against debug()'s at :375`. **A pass-2 seat then read `:375` as a SAME-FILE citation and reported claim 3 as failing**, with a second seat independently flagging one `:NNN` it 'cannot prove cross-file'. **The judgement was refuted by demonstration, which is stronger than any argument I had for it**: the question was never whether the idiom CAN be read correctly but whether it IS, and two of six readers did not. Fixed by repeating the filename rather than relying on proximity. THE RULE SHARPENS: **a citation's qualifier must be ON the citation, not merely NEAR it.** Proximity is not qualification -- it depends on the reader carrying context across a line break, which is exactly what a reader skimming a 60-line comment does not do.open

wdcringambigwdcringambig the wdc inbuf ring uses head==tail for BOTH empty and full with no disambiguator, and its two BULK paths never compare the pointers at allwdcringambig the wdc inbuf ring uses head==tail for BOTH empty and full with no disambiguator, and its two BULK paths never compare the pointers at all — witness: none yet -- a READING, settled by opening dev_wdc.c:139-167, :337-359 and :872-883. The byte-path half is cheap to witness at rung 3 (it is the same access the `wdcflood` :160 witness already drives). The BULK half needs an attached IDE image, so it is gated behind `landiskdisk` like the rest of the wdc disk paths. — note: *** RAISED ON THE `wdcflood` PASS-1 PANEL (panel_20260825_195526) BY THE kimi SEAT -- THE SEAT `panel.sh` HAD STOPPED FIRING. *** It was recovered by hand that same minute after its CLI transport walled (see `panelseatlabel`), and it produced the deepest finding of the panel. The brief asked, as its least-certain premise, whether latching `:160` would HIDE a real defect. agy (file-reading) answered no -- `:160` is a guest error, safe to latch. kimi answered *"your worry is real but located ONE SITE OFF"*. **Settled by reading, not by vote: kimi is right, and the defect is larger than either seat stated.** *** FOUR FACTS, ALL VERIFIED BY OPENING THE FILE. *** (1) `head == tail` IS THE ONLY STATE INDICATOR -- there is no count, no full flag, no spare slot. Verified by grepping every write to `inbuf_head`/`inbuf_tail`: :143, :165, :347, :349, :878 and nothing else. So the ring cannot distinguish EMPTY from FULL. (2) `wdc_addtoinbuf` (:141-146) checks POST-HOC: it stores, advances head, THEN tests `head == tail`. The warning therefore fires when the ring BECOMES full -- and the store that actually CORRUPTS is the NEXT one, which advances head to head+1 != tail and is SILENT. (3) `wdc_get_inbuf` (:157-163) reads `inbuf[tail]` at :157 BEFORE testing anything, then treats `head == tail` as EMPTY. **So after an overrun it reports "someone is reading too much" and returns -1 while 262,656 bytes of valid data sit unreachable in the buffer.** That is `:160`'s predicate becoming unsound -- exactly the shape the brief worried about, one site removed. (4) *** AND THE TWO BULK PATHS BYPASS THE CHECK ENTIRELY. *** `:343-349` advances head by up to `512 * to_read` after comparing ONLY against `WDC_INBUF_SIZE`, the physical end of the array -- it never compares against `tail`, so head can jump straight PAST tail leaving `head != tail` on a grossly overfull ring, with NO warning, because :144's test exists only in the byte-at-a-time path. `:876-879` does the mirror image to `tail`. *** THE CONSEQUENCE FOR `wdcflood`, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY RATHER THAN FOLDED IN: *** latching `:145` and `:160` silences the ONLY two diagnostics this ring has, while the bookkeeping defect goes untouched. The flood fix must therefore not be read as having addressed the ring. Under the reopening rule these are different rounds -- different fix design (a latch versus a state-representation change) and a different oracle (log-line count versus data integrity through the ring). SEVERITY, stated honestly: the byte-path half is a WRONG-DATA path (a guest is told the buffer is empty when it is full), not a host kill. The bulk half is a silent buffer overwrite WITHIN the allocated 262,656 bytes -- `zeroed_alloc(WDC_INBUF_SIZE)` at :1049 -- so it is data corruption, NOT an out-of-bounds host write. That distinction is deliberate and should not be inflated. *** MEASUREMENT OWED BEFORE ANY FIX: *** whether a real guest driver can reach the overrun at all. WDC_MAX_SECTORS is 512, so the ring holds `512*(512+1)` = 262,656 bytes; filling it by guest stores costs ~65,664 32-bit stores, while the bulk disk path fills 512 bytes per sector and would reach it far sooner. That measurement needs `landiskdisk`. *** CORROBORATED BY THREE FURTHER SEATS ON THE SAME PANEL, EACH REACHING IT INDEPENDENTLY AND NONE OF THEM ASKED ABOUT IT DIRECTLY. *** The brief asked only whether latching `:160` would hide a defect. glm: *":145 is an emulator error -- do NOT latch without fixing the ring overrun."* minimax: *":145 IS a real defect that the latch does not fix -- it corrupts the ring and continues, so a TODO is owed there."* grok: *":145 is the unfixed pckbc/asc wrap, not a twin of the measured :160 flood"* -- which additionally suggests the SAME ring-wrap class exists in `dev_pckbc.c` and `dev_asc.c` and is worth a census before this row is worked. **Four of eight seats located a defect the brief did not ask about, at a site the brief named only in passing.** *** A CONSTRAINT THIS ROW WILL NEED, ESTABLISHED 2026-08-25 BY THE kimi SUBSTITUTE SEAT ON THE `wdcflood` PASS-2 PANEL. *** The obvious repair for a ring that cannot distinguish empty from full is the classic WASTE-ONE-SLOT disambiguator. The obvious objection is that this ring is exactly sized -- `WDC_INBUF_SIZE` is `512 * (WDC_MAX_SECTORS + 1)` = 262,656 -- so wasting a slot might break a max-length transfer. **It does not: a max-length transfer is 512 * 512 = 262,144, and 262,144 <= 262,655.** Only the 513-undrained-IDENTIFY fill exceeds the reduced capacity, and that load is the DEFECT'S OWN WITNESS rather than legitimate traffic. Recorded here so the round does not have to re-derive it, and so the objection is answered before it is raised.open

Someone could close that with a bounds guard and **the announce question would vanish with it**, unexamined. Different question, different id. *** THE DISSENT, CARRIED VERBATIM AS PROVENANCE (three seats, independently -- codex and grok file-reading, deepseek packet-fed): *** codex -- *"byte/word probes are distinguishable using `len`, and unaligned calls using `relative_addr`; a predicate such as 'not an aligned 4-byte subaccess' is demonstrably nonempty. Therefore a bounded diagnostic remains viable. Silent fall-through may still be chosen as policy, but this commit has not proved that a latch would announce legal traffic or that every useful handler-local predicate is empty."* deepseek -- *"A byte access to +0x0d is not a lane of a legal multi-word access... the predicate would not be empty; it would select byte accesses to reserved word 3."* grok -- *"The latch FILTER is empty for len=4 in the modelled groups; that does NOT refute the in-tree bounded-announce option."* *** WHAT #463 ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, restated correctly: *** the predicate is empty ONLY for an ALIGNED 32-BIT access at +0x0c, where a legal `fmov.d` half and a direct probe are byte-identical calls at the handler. Every other shape -- byte, word, unaligned -- is distinguishable. The round's record claimed the option was REFUTED; it was not, and that claim is corrected in place in the CHANGELOG and the ledger. *** IT CLEARS THE 'EARNS A ROUND' DISCRIMINATOR, WHICH A DESIGN DISSENT USUALLY DOES NOT: IT STATES A MEASURABLE CONSEQUENCE. *** MEASURED BY READING: `core/debugmsg.c:375` is `if ((quiet_mode && !ss) || v < 0) return;`, and free-running at `verbose == 0` gives v = -1. So a byte probe at +0x0d produces **ZERO host output today**; under a bounded latch it produces N. **That delta IS the self-announcing property the round's own de-escalation clause says the fix destroyed** -- so this is not documented-only, it is a measurable behaviour difference. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENT from the same seat, worth keeping because it is what makes the predicate safe: every multi-word path in this tree decomposes into ALIGNED 4-BYTE lanes only -- `fmov.d` via `cpu->memory_rw(..., sizeof(data), ...)` in all six encodings, and the store queue at `cpu_sh_instr.c:3767-3775` as eight ascending 4-byte calls. So `not an aligned 4-byte subaccess` excludes EVERY lane of EVERY legal multi-word access. *** AND THE THIRD OPTION IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, which is what the THREE-MEMBERED OPTION SET rule was minted from on this very round: *** the fork's house idiom is an N=1 per-instance latch plus `fatal()`, ~34 sites across 11 device files, with the `dev_asc.c:248-257` warrant for keeping `fatal()` over `debugmsg()`. The round debated delete-versus-keep and never costed the third member. DO NOT reopen `#463` for this. The code shipped, is gated and is witnessed; this is a NEW round if it runs at all, ranked by severity against live defects like any other filed item -- and on severity it is insurance, not a live defect.open

gdrompiooddlengdrompiooddlen the GDROM PIO read guards ONE byte and then reads TWO -- LATENT, because no path can produce an odd length todaygdrompiooddlen the GDROM PIO read guards ONE byte and then reads TWO -- LATENT, because no path can produce an odd length today — witness: none, and none is possible today -- the OWED reachability measurement was done BY READING and came back NEGATIVE. The code asymmetry is real; the route to it is not. See the correction below. — note: *** FOUND 2026-08-25 WHILE VERIFYING A PREMISE IN THE `gdrompionull` PASS-1 BRIEF, NOT WHILE LOOKING FOR IT. *** The brief's Q4 asked, almost as an afterthought, whether `d->cur_data_offset` is reset anywhere -- because the round had reasoned about `data_len` throughout and barely looked at the guard's OTHER operand. It is reset (`:327`, beside the NULL). But reading the guard to check that showed something else. *** THE GUARD CHECKS ONE BYTE AND THE BODY READS TWO. *** Verified by reading, three lines: (1) `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:611` -- `if (d->cur_data_offset < d->data_len) {` (2) `:612-613` -- `odata = d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++];` then `odata |= (d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++] << 8);` -- **two increments, one bounds test** (3) `alloc_data` `:309` -- `malloc(d->data_len)`, **exactly `data_len` bytes, no padding, no rounding**. So at `cur_data_offset == data_len - 1` the guard PASSES, the first read is the last valid byte, and **the second read is `d->data[data_len]` -- one byte past the allocation**. *** REACHABILITY, STATED AS WHAT IS READ AND WHAT IS OWED. *** READ: `data_len = d->cnt` (`:307`), and `d->cnt` is GUEST-WRITABLE A BYTE AT A TIME -- `:704` sets the low byte from a CNTLO store and `:712` the high byte from CNTHI, so an ODD count is expressible. The two subsequent adjustments do not remove oddness: `:409-410` only replaces `cnt` when it is ZERO, and `:486-487` only rewrites the single value 65536. **OWED: a measurement that an odd `cnt` actually survives to `alloc_data` on a path a guest can drive.** The existing `gdrom_pio_null_probe.py` already stages commands through these registers and could answer it with two extra stores; I have NOT run it, and this row does not claim the defect is reachable until that runs. *** WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT FROM `gdrompionull` AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. *** That row is `data` NULL while `data_len` lies -- a state-invariant violation whose fix is one assignment in the tail. This is an OFF-BY-ONE in a bounds test, on a path where `data` is a perfectly valid pointer and `data_len` is honest. Different fix design (`< data_len` becomes `+ 1 < data_len`, or the read becomes width-aware), different oracle (a heap over-read, not a SIGSEGV), so under the reopening rule they are separate rounds. **Note the two interact in the safe direction: `gdrompionull`'s fix sets `data_len = 0`, under which this guard is false and the over-read cannot occur on THAT path.** It does nothing for the odd-count path. *** AND UNLIKE THIS DEVICE'S OTHER OUT-OF-BOUNDS ISSUES, ASan SHOULD SEE THIS ONE. *** The file's own comment at `:272` records that ASan cannot detect its member-to-member overrun because that is intra-object inside one malloc. **This is a read PAST a malloc'd buffer's end**, which is the case ASan is built for -- so `build-asan/` is a real second oracle here, where for the aliasing family it was not. That is worth testing early because it is cheap and because a positive ASan result would settle reachability and severity in one run. SEVERITY, stated honestly and NOT inflated: a ONE-BYTE heap over-READ. It does not write, and the byte it returns goes to the guest as the high half of a 16-bit read. That is an information leak of one adjacent heap byte per odd-length transfer and a potential crash only if the allocation ends exactly on a page boundary. It is materially less severe than the SIGSEGV in `gdrompionull` and should rank below it. *** REACHABILITY SETTLED 2026-08-25, THE SAME DAY THIS ROW WAS FILED, AND IT SETTLED AGAINST THE ROW. *** The filing said the odd-count route was OWED and explicitly did NOT claim the defect was reachable. That was the right caution, and the answer is NO. *** `data_len` HAS EXACTLY ONE WRITER, AND BOTH ROUTES TO IT FORCE AN EVEN VALUE. *** Verified by grepping every assignment: `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:307` in `alloc_data` (`d->data_len = d->cnt;`) is the only one -- the apparent second hit at `:413` is a printf FORMAT STRING, not an assignment, which is the kind of match that would have made this look open if counted rather than read. `alloc_data` has exactly two call sites and each is guarded: * `:342`, the Read-TOC path, is preceded by `:338-341` -- `if (d->cnt != 408) { fatal(...); exit(1); }`. **408 is even**, and nothing else reaches this call. * `:418`, the read-sectors path, is preceded by `:412-415` -- `if (sector_count * 2048 != d->cnt) { fatal(...); break; }`. **Any multiple of 2048 is even.** Note `:409-410` only substitutes a count when `cnt == 0`, so a guest-set odd count survives THAT line -- and is then rejected by the equality check two lines later. **So the guest CAN express an odd `cnt` at the CNTLO/CNTHI registers (:704, :712), and that half of the filing was right; what it cannot do is get that value past either guard into `alloc_data`.** *** DISPOSITION: LATENT, NOT LIVE. SEVERITY DROPS FROM A ONE-BYTE HEAP OVER-READ TO A STRUCTURAL HAZARD WITH NO ROUTE. *** The asymmetry itself is untouched and still worth recording: `:611` guards `cur_data_offset < data_len` and `:612-613` reads TWO bytes, while `alloc_data` mallocs exactly `data_len` with no padding. **Any future edit that admits an odd length -- a new command arm, a relaxed guard, a different transfer size -- makes this live immediately, and the code carries nothing that would stop it.** That is a real thing to know and a cheap thing to fix (`+ 1 < data_len`, or make the read width-aware), but it is NOT a defect a guest can reach today and this row may not be ranked as one. *** AND THE ASan NOTE IN THE FILING IS NOW MOOT AND IS WITHDRAWN. *** It said `build-asan/` would be a real second oracle here, unlike the intra-object aliasing family. True in principle and irrelevant in fact: ASan cannot observe an access no execution reaches. *Process note worth keeping: this row was filed with reachability marked OWED rather than asserted, and the owed check refuted it within the hour -- at the cost of two greps. Had it been filed as a live heap over-read it would have been a WRONG RECORD ranked above real work, and the correction would have arrived later and cost more.*open

wdcperopcodewdcperopcode wdc_command()'s unimplemented-command latch is per-DEVICE, so a guest cycling opcodes gets ONE line and 255 silent aborts -- a SPEC choice, filed not fixedwdcperopcode wdc_command()'s unimplemented-command latch is per-DEVICE, so a guest cycling opcodes gets ONE line and 255 silent aborts -- a SPEC choice, filed not fixed — witness: n/a -- this is a SPEC improvement, not a defect. The shipped behaviour is deliberate and is pinned by the `unimpl 2op` row, which fires TWO different opcodes and demands ONE line. — note: *** FILED 2026-08-26 BECAUSE THE SHIPPED DETECTOR'S CONTRACT CLAIMED A FILING THAT DID NOT EXIST. *** `wdc_flood_probe.py`'s header says *"deepseek argued for a per-opcode set; FILED, not shipped"* -- and no row carried it; the only trace was prose inside `wdcflood`'s state_note, which is not something a reader can find. **A contract line asserting a disposition is a WRONG RECORD until the disposition exists as a row.** Caught by the readiness adjudication before the round shipped. THE PROPOSAL, from the deepseek seat on the `wdcflood` pass-1 panel: `:583`'s diagnostic VALUE is the opcode, so a single per-device flag suppresses every later unimplemented command and hides distinct guest actions. A 256-bit set (`uint32_t warned_unimpl_cmd[8]`) is cheap and preserves them. WHY IT WAS NOT SHIPPED, and the reason is not that it is wrong: the scalar is exactly what stops a guest cycling 0x00..0xff for 256 lines, which is the flood the round exists to bound. Per-opcode-versus-per-device is a SPEC choice between two acceptable behaviours, and the adjudication ruled that clause (d) tests the CHOSEN spec's repair rather than adjudicating between specs -- deepseek's framing ("the scalar IS the (d) mutant") is circular, since it assumes per-opcode is the baseline and then calls the alternative a weakening. *** THE SHIPPED SPEC IS PINNED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE TO DEFER: *** the `unimpl 2op` row fires TWO DIFFERENT opcodes and demands ONE line, so a later change to per-opcode is a VISIBLE spec change that reddens a row, not a silent drift. The same row kills a "last-warned-opcode" latch (measured: `M3`, 21/22, that row alone), under which an alternating guest floods forever. IF IT IS EVER WORKED, the option set is THREE-membered and the third member is the one the dispute never named: scalar (shipped), per-opcode set (deepseek), and the in-tree COUNT-BOUND idiom (`n_trunc_msgs`, `src/cpus/memory_rw.c:495-523`). Note also that #337's other latched messages at `:816`/`:855` carry NO value payload, so "three latches in this file" is weaker precedent for discarding value-resolution than it looks -- `:583` is the only site whose message names an opcode.open

The catch-up CAP is the protection; the ceiling is domain normalisation. Also: the report belongs at the CLAMP SITE (device context, where fatal() is already idiom), not in the handler - and the SIGALRM hazard codex worried about does not exist there. NaN is caught by NEGATING the comparisons that must exist anyway, at zero marginal cost: A FREE GUARD AT A TRUST BOUNDARY NEEDS NO REACHABILITY PROOF. Committed against shipping the loop bound alone, because interval=0 would then burn the cap every signal for ever. — evidence: pipeline/evidence/n2/research/fable5_2026-08-16.md✓2026-08-16 — CONFIRMED — MEASURED EVERYTHING, AND OVERTURNED TWO PROPOSALS. Built the offline driver and proved timer.c CAN be driven in the diff_*.c idiom (one stub: gettimeofday). CENSUS: emulated_hz is an int, so INT_MAX bounds every legitimate request - the ceiling is DERIVED, not picked. POLICY TABLE: 'drop missed ticks' is NOT A POLICY BUT A DEFECT (it caps every timer at 65 Hz - a 100 Hz timer runs at rate 0.65 with no burst at all); the flagship's cap of 65536 BREAKS a legitimate 4e7 Hz timer (1.0000 -> 0.1065); 2^20 is the smallest power of two that leaves every legitimate case BIT-IDENTICAL to shipped. And clamping at :137 alone is not just insufficient but A REGRESSION - it loses idempotence on five of six classes because the early-out then compares a clamped record against a raw request. Caught its own first probe (it held time fixed and would have cleared the defect). — evidence: pipeline/evidence/n2/research/opus_measured_2026-08-16.md✓2026-08-16 — MANUAL — NORMALISE AND REPORT excessive rates rather than silently clamping; guard intervals; bound the catch-up; clamp RTC values BEFORE narrowing to int. Research (fix proposals)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — TWO SIDE QUESTIONS SETTLED, and both corrections went in the direction that keeps the substance. (1) THE ASan CLAIM: refuted on its premise, upheld on its conclusion, and a THIRD reason found that neither I nor the reporting seat had. build_asan.sh:38-39 does set -fsanitize=address,undefined, and the artifact carries eleven __ubsan_handle_* imports INCLUDING __ubsan_handle_add_overflow -- the exact handler an int++ overflow calls. So 'no -fsanitize flag' is false; the seat had grepped the CONSUMER (gate_asan_sweep.sh) rather than the PRODUCER. *** But gate 9 still cannot catch this, and the reason I gave (timeout 25 vs a 42.95 s floor) was only half of it: DEVINIT(footbridge) NEVER CREATES A struct timer AT ALL. *** Only a guest write to TIMER_x_LOAD or TIMER_x_CONTROL|ENABLE does, and a construction sweep runs no guest -- so timer_tick0 is never called and the counter never increments, timeout or no timeout. Either reason alone is fatal. (2) THE '~7.9 s FOR FOUR TIMERS' FIGURE: confirmed impossible, and the seat found WHERE THE NUMBER CAME FROM, which is better than refuting it. 2^31 / (4 x 1048576 x 65) = 7.876 s -- the single-element floor divided by four. The counters are per-timer (:73), each callback increments its own element (:86-92), and the catch-up budget is per-timer too (timer.c:281, inside the per-timer loop), so four timers overflow four DIFFERENT elements at their own rates. True floors: 42.950 s cats (2^31/50,000,000, machine_cats.c:56-57) now measured three times at 43.03/43.10/44.58, and 33.686 s netwinder (2^31/63,750,000, machine_netwinder.c:56). ONE REFINEMENT worth recording: a hard floor of 31.51 s exists from the catch-up ceiling (2^31/68,157,440), but it needs a timer at or above 68.16 MHz, which neither machine's emulated_hz permits. cats's is guarded by `if (== 0)` so a config-file emulated_hz word could reach it; netwinder's is unconditional. Neither is guest-reachable, so severity is unchanged. — evidence: build_asan.sh:38-39; nm of /tmp/gx-asan-head/gxemul; timer.c:281; machine_cats.c:56-57·······

The first port table used CONSECUTIVE LBAs (0x100..0x107), which caught that mutant BY ACCIDENT -- port n's address hit port n-1's entry. Scattering the LBAs to close a DIFFERENT hole (a masked top bit no row could see) SILENTLY REMOVED THAT ACCIDENTAL COVERAGE, and only re-running the whole census after the fixture change surfaced it. That is a general lesson worth more than the row: A FIXTURE CHANGE CAN DELETE COVERAGE NOBODY KNEW THEY HAD, and no row goes red to say so. Closed by F17, which asserts the block boundary EXPLICITLY -- first byte in, last byte in, byte below, byte above, per port -- instead of relying on an occupied neighbour. F17 is currently the ONLY row defending that property. (a) The STALL remains the primary behavioural cost, and for automation it turns an immediate nonzero exit into a possible timeout. Right conclusion, wrong reason, and this project has a recorded case of a wrong reason being cited twice before anyone opened the file. (2) The aliasing claim was PRESENT-TENSE and is only LATENT: `r = 0` at :121 is immediately followed by `exit(1)` at :122, so it is dead code today and 0x08 never enters the block; the hazard activates only if a later edit widens the guard while KEEPING the block. *** AND IT SUPPLIED THE CRUX THE BRIEF MISSED: `r` IS A LIVE ARRAY INDEX *** -- pending_irq[r], mask_13[r], mask_11[r], mask_9[r] -- so the guard is a bounds check that is UNREACHABLE, NOT ABSENT. THE NOTE: if anyone re-raises this against an above-floor detector, the doctrine says it FILES as coverage debt, not drops; keep the licensing ground straight.✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — CHECKED RATHER THAN ARGUED, because the m88k panel split on this row and I recorded that it was checkable. The answer is SPLIT and both halves matter. HALF REFUTED: the filing says the spy 'counts CALLBACK calls'. It does not merely count. diff_m8invread.c:117-133 captures the RECEIVER, the ADDRESS and the FLAGS of every call, and derives inv_all_were_ALL / inv_all_addr_zero / inv_cpu_mismatch from them. Its own comment names exactly the hazard the row raises -- 'a detector that counts calls and ignores their arguments is green for any argument -- the constblind shape, and mutant A walks straight through it'. So the count-only weakness was already found and fixed by an earlier round, and the row's premise is stale on that point. HALF CONFIRMED, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: the detector observes the CALLBACK, never the resulting STATE. `grep -n 'patc\|PATC' regress/diff_m8invread.c` returns NOTHING -- no row inspects the PATC at all. So a mutant that reaches (or fails to reach) the same invalidation by ANY route other than the callback is invisible to every row in the file. That is the row's essential claim and it stands. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SPLIT: the two packet-fed seats ranked this first on vacuity grounds and they were right that a gap exists; the two file-reading seats ranked m8patc first as the only SEMANTIC fix, and that is untouched by this. Both readings survive -- what is now settled is that the gap is REAL, so if this row is worked the round is 'assert the PATC state, not only the callback', not 'stop counting calls'. — evidence: regress/diff_m8invread.c:117-133✓2026-08-20 — MANUAL — WALL DISCHARGED -- re-fired 2026-08-20 after codex answered a health test (CODEX_ALIVE_20260820, and it got the arithmetic right). asicdeclineasicdecline #463b: an explicit decline at r == 3 is an ANCHOR that closes the whole translation class using rows already shippedasicdecline #463b: an explicit decline at r == 3 is an ANCHOR that closes the whole translation class using rows already shipped — MERGED INTO `asicindexcase` and dropped as a DUPLICATE, on the adjudication that reversed its own prior ruling. Filed on an earlier ruling that said 'the line goes in as a new round #463b'; a subsequent CHECK of the function's common tail inverted the dissent's factual core, and the adjudicator then ruled: **no bounds hole exists, the decline already happens through the switch's structure, and the surviving argument (enforcement vs assertion) IS `asicindexcase` wearing a design-review hat.** A dissent whose target is already filed ENRICHES that item rather than spawning a duplicate. Kept as a dropped row, not deleted, so the reversal is visible. — witness: MEASURED DISCRIMINATOR NAMED, NOT YET RUN: `+2` is predicted 13/13 (a clean-sweep escape) on the shipped build and red-by-`safe 4` with the line. Test-first requires measuring that red BEFORE the line lands. — note: FILED 2026-08-25 from #463's RESEARCH STAGE, which was fired to close a panel gap after the round had already committed. **The owner was offered an exemption for the gap and DECLINED it in favour of firing the seats -- this item exists only because of that.** THE SPLIT: six seats. glm and agy defended the shipped deletion; deepseek, minimax, kimi-k3 and opus5 said it is one line short. *** BUT THE VOTE IS NOT THE REASON. *** Two of the defending arguments do not survive: glm's headline ('did not trade a loud failure for a silent one') is contradicted by #463's OWN L4 correction -- the deleted `fatal()` printed unconditionally, the surviving `debug()` is silenced by `-q` and silent free-running at verbose 0 -- and agy's objections ('phantom hardware state', 'architectural inconsistency') aim at the `[4]` and clamp options, not at the decline. *** WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A ROUND IS AN ANCHOR PROPERTY NO SEAT NAMED, and it is arithmetic anyone can check: `if (r == 3) <decline>` pins the DECLINE COLUMN at `(addr & 0x0c) == 0x0c`, so a TRANSLATION MOVES that column onto a probed offset and an EXISTING accept row reddens. *** Verified: `+1` -> declines at +0x08/+0x18/+0x38, reddening `safe 8`, `alias2`, `mask9 rt`; `+2` -> +0x04/+0x24, reddening `safe 4` and `crossarr`; `-1` -> +0x10, reddening `asic ok`. **The whole translation group closes with one line and rows already shipped -- including `+2`, which the shipped contract currently DISCLOSES as unpinned and which escapes even `mask9 rt`.** SECOND GROUND, from the de-escalation membership test: apply an added indexing `case 0x2c:` to the PRE-FIX code and the developer's first test access dies on the old `exit(1)` -- announced during development. Under the shipped code the same edit is a silent member-overlap OOB. That is the class the carrier already names, and control flow is the only enforcement that does not depend on a future editor reading a comment. *** THE FORM IS UNSETTLED AND IS WITH THE ADJUDICATOR. *** A bare `return` is NOT correct as written -- the function has a common tail (`if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memory_writemax64(...); return 1;`) that an early return SKIPS, leaving a guest read with an untouched buffer. Three seats proposed exactly that without reading nine lines down. opus5 proposed decline PLUS a one-shot latch WITH the write-back, citing in-tree precedent neither the round nor the adjudicator had: **`memory_rw.c:495-523`, in the file that DISPATCHES to this device, bounds a guest-drivable diagnostic to 8 emissions via `n_trunc_msgs`, reasoning that 'probing at the end of a device's mapped range is common and benign'.** The fork's own answer to this phenomenon was BOUND THE COUNT, KEEP THE MESSAGE -- #463 chose between keeping it unlatched and deleting it and never saw the third option. CONSTRAINTS THE ROUND MUST MEET: the decline's observable signature must be IDENTICAL to `default:`'s (odata, write-back, return status), and the diagnostic must not be LOST -- an early return skips `default:`'s print and would make r==3 traffic MORE silent than today. Run with prediction-first discipline: **'identical everywhere' is NOT the expected result** -- the translation mutants must go STRICTLY redder, and if they do not, the anchor argument is refuted. **KEEP `mask9 rt`**: it is the only anchor that survives if someone deletes the line, and the two catch the class through different channels. NOT L-LICENSED, and deliberately so: no floor breach, no undischarged obligation (`mask9 rt` closed the L3), no wrong record. Reopening a closed round on 'four seats think it is one line short' is the runaway chain with a jury attached. *** DROPPED 2026-08-25, SAME DAY, BY THE ADJUDICATION THAT REVERSED ITSELF. *** This row existed for roughly one hour on the strength of a ruling that the line should ship as its own round. Reading the function's common tail then showed the dissent's factual core was false, and the adjudicator withdrew the ruling. Recorded rather than erased: **a filed item created and dropped inside one session is what a fast reversal looks like, and hiding it would make the queue look steadier than the reasoning was.**dropped

The program gen_dashboard.py makes this page from pipeline/ledger.json. Do not change this page manually. If a cell does not have a ledger entry, the cell is a defect. A packet-fed seat examines the argument only. Its vote about the contents of the repository is not equal to the vote of a seat that reads files (PIPELINE.md, Section 1). An ✕ cell can be the most important cell in its row: the ✕ in the Research phase of #419 changed the design. Rule for closed rows (owner, 2026-08-15): a closed row does not need new tests when the flagship seat (Fable) examined the final change and its evidence. That examination fills the Final review cell of the closed row. Regression phase (owner, 2026-08-15): only the flagship seat reviews the regression tests, and the reviews are BATCHED TO SUNDAY NIGHT, after the full battery, which now runs Sunday at 18:00 so that its evidence covers the rounds the review examines. The other eight cells in a Regression line are NOT REQUIRED, and a Regression line that is empty on a round finished after Saturday is WAITING FOR THE SUNDAY BATCH, not missing. So a line of dots there shows a rule, not a gap. The first three phases still need all nine seats, per round, before that round proceeds.
